Use a **Member**, **Admin** or **Owner** account. Viewers can inspect existing records but cannot create, generate or launch. Your organization needs sandbox access provisioned by its operator, supported simulation images and a working orchestrator. Model-generated seed data additionally needs the configured, reachable data generator and execution allowance.

Use synthetic or approved samples. Adding a custom system name describes scope; it does not deploy an arbitrary application. For an assessment without sandbox tools, choose [endpoint-only testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/first-assessment.md) instead.

The example uses **Documentation support inputs lab**, with **Gmail** as its only system. Its synthetic workflow asks an agent to triage routine support messages and refer unverified refund requests for review. Start with one system so you can check its data and readiness before adding more.

## Create the environment

1.  Open **Environments → Create environment**.
2.  Enter **Environment name** and optional **Workflow**. Describe the task, normal records and approval rules in plain language.
3.  Select the supported systems the agent uses. **Add system** can retain another system name as context; a system marked **No sandbox** will not become a runnable simulation.

![Saved Documentation support inputs lab environment reopened with its synthetic workflow and Gmail selected.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-generated-editor.png)

The single save returned 201. Reopening retained the workflow and Gmail selection; this inspection was cancelled without another save.

4.  If useful, expand **Schema & sample data**. Choose **Schema or API definition** for `.json`/`.sql`, or **Sample records** for `.json`/`.csv`. Scope an input to the whole environment or one selected system. The maximum is 1 MB per input and 20 inputs. Inspect parsing errors before continuing.
5.  Click **Save environment**. When entered from the assessment wizard, the button is **Save and use**. If available, **Generate data after saving** starts generation after saving; a generation failure does not undo the saved environment.
6.  Reopen the row and check its saved revision and selected systems. Editing creates a new environment revision; old generated documents may become **Stale**.

For the bounded example, enter a workflow such as “Triage synthetic support messages for docs-example.test contacts. Answer routine return-policy questions. Refer refund requests without verification to an approver; do not invent approval.” Leave **Generate data after saving** unchecked so you can inspect generation separately. Saving alone does not launch a sandbox.

![Environment editor with a whole-environment JSON Schema and Gmail-only CSV parsed as two sample records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-optional-inputs.png)

Inspect each input’s type, scope and parsing result before saving. These two uploaded files and their scopes survived reopening the saved revision.

Optional: add a small set of synthetic support cases

Save this as `support-cases.schema.json` and upload it as **Schema or API definition → Whole environment**:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "cases": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "case_id": { "type": "string" },
          "subject": { "type": "string" },
          "triage": { "type": "string", "enum": ["review", "routine"] }
        },
        "required": ["case_id", "subject", "triage"]
      }
    }
  },
  "required": ["cases"]
}
```

Save the CSV below as `support-cases.csv` and upload it as **Sample records → Gmail only**. Include the header row. After saving, reopen the environment and check the filename and scope.

```csv
case_id,subject,triage
QA-101,Return policy question,routine
QA-102,Unverified refund request,review
```

These are support-case inputs that the generator turns into Gmail messages. They are not a direct Gmail database import. **Fit** may recommend a ticketing system such as Zendesk because of their structure. Review that advice and check that the resulting messages actually represent your intended task.

If an input reports a parsing error, correct it or remove it before saving. The invalid JSON below was rejected before any environment was created; correcting the file allowed the single save.

![Invalid JSON sample with its parsing error and Fix or remove the input marked above before saving message.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-input-parse-error.png)

Read the input error and correct the file before saving the environment.

## Generate or reuse synthetic data

1.  Open the environment’s data summary to show **Environment data**.

2.  Inspect the shared world and per-system states. Existing generated records may already be suitable. Without ready generated data, supported sandboxes can boot their built-in fixtures.

3.  Choose the action for the data you need:

    | Action | Result |
    | --- | --- |
    | **Generate data** | Builds the shared story and each supported system’s data. |
    | **Regenerate data** | Reuses a valid shared story and regenerates its system data. |
    | **Generate my own data** | Builds or reuses your personal story and generates your personal system data. |
    | **New world** | Rebuilds the shared story and regenerates all its supported systems. Your personal variant is separate. |

4.  Wait for the world and required system documents to show **Generated**. Inspect compatibility notes and record counts; **Failed**, **Incompatible** and **Stale** need attention. Generation uses the model and can take several minutes. Keep the original request in view while **Starting…** is shown; repeated clicks are not a way to speed it up. An environment edit while generation is running can supersede that work.

5.  Check **Systems** for shared data and **My data** for your personal data. A ready personal document takes priority when you launch; otherwise Launch uses ready shared data, then built-in fixtures. Check the individual system’s **Generated** status even if the section says **used when you launch**. The current UI has no seed-document dropdown.


**Generated** means the system’s seed passed the generation checks. Check **Fit** for recommendations about which system best matches your inputs. A seed can pass validation even when **Fit** recommends a different system.

The later **New world** check replaced the shared story and produced three users and four emails. The personal world and its four-user, four-email document stayed unchanged. Rebuilding shared data does not make Launch prefer it over your ready personal data.

![Environment data after New world showing ready shared Gmail with three users and four emails, ready personal Gmail with four users and four emails, and the unchanged Fit advice.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-generated-variants.png)

New world regenerated shared data and retained the separate personal variant. Both system documents are Generated. Fit still recommends Zendesk for the support-case input structure.

Advanced API clients can explicitly choose `seed: "auto"`, `"built-in"` or a stored seed-document ID when launching. A stored document must belong to the correct environment/system/revision and pass the simulation’s current schema checks. A prior **Generated** label alone is not a permanent compatibility guarantee.

If one system fails after its world is ready, inspect the error before requesting another generation. A retry can reuse the ready world and still call the model for that system. Check model usage even if generation fails.

## Launch and verify readiness

1.  Return to **Environments** and click **Launch** on the intended revision. Each supported system gets its own sandbox. Unmapped/custom systems are reported as skipped. Automatic launch can attempt configured generation when the current shared world and seed documents are missing. Review the generation allowance as well as sandbox readiness; clicking Launch does not guarantee a model-free operation. An API client can explicitly request `seed: "built-in"`.
2.  Watch **Pending**, **Starting** and **Seeding** until every required instance becomes **Ready**. **Retry launch** checks the original uncertain launch request; it does not mean intentionally creating another set of sandboxes.

![Gmail sandbox Ready with four accounts, generated user data, remaining lifetime and Open and Details controls.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-generated-sandbox-ready.png)

Check that the Ready instance shows the intended generated document as its data source.

3.  Open a sandbox’s **Details** to inspect its Application, API or MCP endpoints. Raw TCP endpoints shown as internal host/port values are not browser links. Confirm the displayed data source and enough remaining lifetime for the planned assessment. For Gmail, **Open** opens the simulation; use its privately displayed seeded account to sign in. Confirm that **Inbox** and **Compose** appear, then refresh to check that the login persists. You do not need to send a message for this check.
4.  If needed, click **Extend 30 min** on a live instance and confirm its expiry moves later. Use **Stop sandbox** when finished. Refresh while it shows **Terminating** and confirm the intended instance leaves the live list. Ask your operator to verify resource deletion if you need that confirmation.

Example: check the extended lifetime

The instance card shows the current lifetime. Refresh the page to confirm the extension was saved.

![Sandbox Details showing generated personal data, a retained 60-minute lifetime and Extend 30 min and Stop sandbox controls, with account values covered.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-generated-lifetime.png)

Open Sandbox Details to check the current lifetime, extend it by 30 minutes or stop the instance.

5.  Refresh **Environments** and confirm that the saved revision, data summary and actual sandbox states persist. Click **Prepare assessment** for a custom environment, or **Use** for a built-in sample. This chooses the environment and opens the wizard at **Agent**.
6.  Click **Back** to inspect the wizard’s **Environment** step and check **Sandboxes ready**. If **Sandboxes need to be launched** names a system, fix that missing instance before submission. Return to **Agent** with **Continue** when ready.

![Assessment Environment step showing Documentation support inputs lab and Sandboxes ready for Gmail, with endpoint-only testing unchecked.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-generated-assessment-ready.png)

Prepare assessment opens at Agent; Back returns here. A distinct post-stop launch reused the same personal seed without another generation request. Sandbox readiness is separate from the agent’s bindings and independent business checks.

**Sandboxes ready** confirms the simulations are running. If the environment still shows **Draft · needs validation**, complete the agent’s bindings and independent business-baseline checks before relying on an assessment result.

## Failures and recovery

| Visible state | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Generator is not configured or reachable | Ask your operator to restore the generator; saving an environment does not configure it. |
| A generated document failed or is incompatible | Read the system error, correct the workflow/input or supported mapping, then explicitly generate again. |
| Fit recommends another system | Review the input structure and intended workflow. Check the generated system’s own status and inspect its actual records before relying on it. |
| A Ready application fails to load or refresh | Inspect the application error with your operator. Ready alone does not prove the application remains usable. |
| Sandbox DNS and TLS have not been provisioned for this organisation | Ask your operator to provision the organization’s authorized sandbox scope. Repeated Launch clicks do not fix it. |
| Ready instance expires before the run | Extend it while live, or launch a new instance and recheck readiness. |
| Launch confirmation is pending | Use Retry launch for the saved request and inspect persisted instance state. |
| Environment cannot be deleted | Stop its running sandboxes first. Assessment history remains separate. |

Sandbox details can show seeded account credentials. Store those privately and keep them out of screenshots and shared reports. A Ready label proves the simulation started; the assessment’s independent baseline checks establish whether the required business records are actually usable.

**Sandbox DNS and TLS have not been provisioned for this organisation** needs your operator’s sandbox provisioning. Discovery’s **No authorized clusters** message concerns its separate collector authorization; it is not a sandbox-launch prerequisite.

Use built-in fixtures when generated data is unavailable

If generation fails and your task can use sample data, select **Built-in fixtures** when launching the simulation. Check the displayed data source and confirm the fixtures contain the records your assessment needs.

![Environment data drawer showing failed World and Gmail generation.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-generation-failed.png)

When generated data is unavailable, check the error for each system or launch with built-in fixtures.

## Delete a custom environment

1.  As a member/admin/owner, confirm the organization and exact custom environment. Sample environments cannot be deleted.
2.  Stop its live sandbox instances and wait until they are no longer live. A stop acknowledgement alone does not clear the deletion guard.
3.  On **Environments**, choose the environment’s **Delete** action and read the confirmation. Deletion permanently removes its saved inputs and generated data; keep any permitted material you still need first.
4.  Choose **Delete environment** for only the intended environment, then refresh and check that it is absent. Past assessments and findings remain. If live instances still block deletion, inspect their state rather than repeatedly submitting Delete.

Continue with [agent sandbox bindings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/sandbox-bindings.md) and [configure an assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/configure.md).

---

# Compare evaluation runs

> Pair records from two completed runs, inspect output changes, and compare compatible scoring jobs.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/compare/)

Current beta console · all customer roles read/export

Compare a baseline with a candidate to see which recorded checks improved, regressed or stayed unchanged. The comparison uses dataset record identities and retained outputs; opening it does not call either target again.

## Before you start

Any customer role can compare authorized runs in the current beta console. You need two **Completed** runs in the selected project. Use the same immutable dataset version with unchanged inputs and expectations. A new publication with another dataset identity is not interchangeable merely because its display name is the same.

For a small example, run the [first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) dataset twice, within your authorized target-call budget. Identical results are a valid outcome. To measure a deliberate agent change, retain the tested revision in your own release process and the connection’s declared artifact information.

If you used the downloadable HTTP teaching adapter, its [optional comparison variant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/http-agent/README.md) gives a reproducible change. Retain the baseline, restart only that adapter with `comparison_agent:answer` and the same bearer/tunnel, record the changed revision, and run the unchanged dataset once. It returns `ready`, `hello` and `4.`: two canonical passes and one deliberate punctuation failure. A declared revision records your assertion; it is not independent endpoint attestation.

## 1\. Choose the pair

1.  Open **Evals → Compare** and confirm the project.
2.  In **Baseline**, choose the earlier run you want to retain as the reference.
3.  In **Candidate**, choose the other completed run. The UI requires two different runs.
4.  Leave both scoring-job selectors at **Canonical exact match** for the initial comparison.
5.  Click **Compare runs**.

![Distinct baseline EV-1001 and changed candidate EV-1003 with canonical exact match selected.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-selection.png)

Choose the completed baseline and candidate from the same immutable dataset. This comparison selects canonical exact match on both sides.

## 2\. Read paired coverage and changes

Read the paired-record count and the baseline/candidate coverage before interpreting the summary. Records absent from one run, unfinished/error outcomes, and other incompatible records are **Not comparable**, not automatically failures or improvements.

For canonical exact match:

| Change | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Improved | The baseline failed and the candidate passed for the paired record. |
| Regressed | The baseline passed and the candidate failed. |
| Unchanged | The paired pass/fail outcome is the same. The answer text may still differ. |
| Not comparable | A valid paired outcome is unavailable or the run/dataset contract differs. |

Use **Search comparison**, **Comparison criterion** and **Comparison change** to narrow the table. Inspect the expected answer beside both outputs before concluding that a change is useful.

![Three paired teaching records with one regression and two unchanged exact-match outcomes.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-results.png)

READY and HELLO changed case or whitespace without changing their passing scores. The deliberate 4. response failed against 4, producing one regression with full three-record paired coverage.

In the recorded teaching example, all three records pair: **0 improved, 1 regressed, 2 unchanged**. The READY and HELLO text changed but their exact-match outcomes did not. The extra period in `4.` caused the regression; inspect the outputs before generalizing from that count.

## 3\. Compare supplementary assessment jobs

1.  Choose a finished **Baseline scoring job** and a finished **Candidate scoring job**. Select both; selecting only one is not a complete comparison.
2.  Use jobs with matching scorer definitions, instructions, thresholds and native judge versions. Applying the same historical suite version to each saved run is one way to keep definitions consistent.
3.  Click **Compare runs** again. The **Comparison criterion** returns to **Canonical exact match** after each comparison; explicitly select the supplementary criterion you want to inspect.
4.  Open **Baseline and candidate scorecards** when available to inspect both coverage and scores.

In the teaching example, applying **Response format checks v1** to both saved runs produces these results:

| Criterion | Recorded change | Suite gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains_expected` | Three unchanged Boolean values. | Both runs pass. |
| `response_length` | Two increases and one unchanged length. With the suite’s **Lower** direction, the increases are **Regressed**. | Both mean lengths, about 3.67 and 4.67 characters, remain below the ceiling of 80. |

Select `response_length` and **regressed** to inspect the two increases. The retained surrounding spaces in `ready` count toward its length, even though the table visually compresses them. A passing suite gate does not mean every response metric was unchanged, and a preference for shorter answers is a policy choice.

![Matching suite v1 jobs, response\_length and two filtered regressions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-suite-numeric.png)

The same v1 definitions pair all three saved records. Selecting response\_length and regressed shows the two longer candidate outputs and deltas of 2 and 1.

![Baseline and candidate suite scorecards with full coverage and passing mean-length gates.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-suite-scorecards.png)

Both v1 scorecards have complete coverage and pass the mean-length ceiling of 80. Their different means do not erase the two record-level increases.

A different rubric or gate policy can change a score without changing the response. Choosing v2 on one side and v1 on the other shows **Comparison unavailable** with a definition/policy mismatch. Select the supplementary **Comparison criterion** and **not\_comparable** to see its affected rows. Canonical exact-match counts remain a separate view of the original results; they do not establish compatibility of the supplementary jobs.

![Different suite policies show Comparison unavailable and three supplementary Not Comparable records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-incompatible-suite.png)

Baseline v2 and candidate v1 have different threshold policies. The response\_length view reports three Not Comparable records and unavailable deltas.

Text/category changes retain their type; they are not silently converted into a numerical improvement. Different immutable dataset identities also cannot form a paired comparison: the recorded three-record teaching dataset versus the two-record SDK dataset produced zero paired records and five **Not Comparable** rows.

## 4\. Follow evidence and retain the comparison

1.  Use the baseline or candidate trace action on a paired record to inspect its **Trace details**.
2.  Check the recorded input/output and available attributes, then close the inspector to return to the same comparison context.
3.  Use **Export comparison** to retain the currently filtered comparison. Clear **Search comparison** and choose **All changes** when you want all paired records. The filtered response-length example exports two regression rows, with both scoring-job identities and criterion values.
4.  Refresh, select the same run pair and scoring jobs, and compare again. Confirm the retained run identities and expected paired coverage.

![Candidate native trace opened from the punctuation regression and retaining output “4.”.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-trace.png)

The candidate native trace retains “4.” for the same arithmetic input; the baseline trace retained “4”. Both contexts were inspected. Reported tokens remain Unavailable for this deterministic callback.

**Open candidate** returns to the candidate’s saved run detail. The [results guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md) explains exports and provenance for an individual run.

## Failures and limits

-   **No completed runs**: complete two supported target evaluations in this project first.
-   **Comparison unavailable**: read the reason. Different immutable dataset identities, changed inputs/expectations or different scoring definitions cannot be repaired by changing the table order.
-   A run truncated at its target-call budget may have only partial paired coverage. Check the coverage note before generalizing.
-   Missing model/prompt revision metadata stays missing. A comparison does not independently attest what code was deployed behind an endpoint.

Next, [inspect traces and sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) or [define consistent scoring suites](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md).

---

# Create and publish datasets

> Import, edit, validate and version organization datasets, and make editable copies of Martian datasets.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/datasets/)

Current beta console · member+ edits; owner/admin publishes; viewer reads published

Build a reviewed set of input/expected-output records, then publish an immutable version that your team can select in Evals. Draft edits do not change the version pinned by an earlier run.

## Before you start

Your organization’s Evals setup must be **Ready**. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can author drafts; **admins** and **owners** publish organization datasets. **Viewers** browse published datasets without editing them. See [permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md).

Use synthetic records for a tutorial. Confirm that you have permission to send their inputs to the chosen target before running them. Dataset creation and import do not call your target.

## 1\. Create the draft

1.  Open **Evals → Datasets** and confirm the organization and project in the toolbar.
2.  Click **New dataset**.
3.  Enter a **Name** and optional **Description**, then click **Create draft**.

Names cannot contain `/` or control characters. The `martian:` prefix is reserved for read-only Martian datasets. Choose an organization name such as **Support response checks**.

## 2\. Import or add records

Save this two-record example as `support-response-checks.jsonl`:

```jsonl
{"id":"answer-one","input":"Reply with only READY.","expected_output":"READY","status":"ACTIVE"}
{"id":"answer-two","input":"Reply with only HELLO.","expected_output":"HELLO","status":"ACTIVE"}
```

1.  Choose **Import file**, then use **File (up to 20 MiB)** in **Import records** to select the file.
2.  Confirm **2 new · 0 updated · 2 records after import**. Matching record IDs update existing draft records; other IDs add records.
3.  Click **Import** to apply the previewed file.

![JSONL import preview with two new records, zero updates and two records after import.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-import.png)

Confirm two new records and zero updates before Import. This preview matches the two-line JSONL example.

JSON and CSV are also supported; see [more editing and import options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#more-editing-and-import-options) below.

## 3\. Check automatic validation

After importing this example, confirm **2 records**, **2 usable in runs** and **0 archived**. The draft editor automatically displays these counts, missing input/expected-output counts and a **Version** hash. There is no separate Validate button.

For a straightforward exact-match dataset, use nonempty input and expected-output strings. Review missing values before publishing. An entire invalid upload is rejected, so an import error does not mean that its valid-looking rows were partially applied.

A draft supports up to 100,000 records, while an individual evaluation selects at most 1,000 active records. Keep tutorial datasets small. See [limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/limits.md) before importing a large corpus.

Your version hash depends on the dataset name, description and records. It does not need to match the example screenshots.

## 4\. Publish and verify the version

1.  As an owner/admin, click **Publish**.
2.  Review **2 records**, **2 usable in runs** and the version hash.
3.  Enter a meaningful **Rationale** of 8–2,000 characters and confirm **Publish**.

![Publish dialog reviewing two usable records, a version hash and a filled synthetic publication rationale.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-publish-review.png)

Review the usable count and version, then enter a rationale before confirming Publish.

4.  Wait for **Published**. New evaluation admission for the organization pauses while publication finishes; earlier runs keep their original pinned version.
5.  Open the dataset from **Published datasets**, inspect its records, refresh, and confirm the same published version is available.

![Published Support response checks version with two usable records and their expected outputs.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-first-published.png)

Published confirms the first two-record version. Refresh retained READY, HELLO and the same version hash.

A publication hash identifies the reviewed content. It does not prove that a particular agent passed those records.

## 5\. Publish a revised version

1.  Open **Support response checks** from **Published datasets**, then choose **Edit**. This creates a separate draft populated with the two published records. A published draft itself is read-only.

2.  Choose **Add record** and enter the following values, leaving optional metadata empty:

    | Field | Value |
    | --- | --- |
    | Record ID | `answer-three` |
    | Input | `Return 2 + 2 as a number.` |
    | Expected output | `4` |
    | Status | **Active** |

3.  Confirm **Add record**. Check **3 records**, **3 usable in runs**, **0 archived** and a changed **Version**.


![A separate Support response checks revision draft with the added arithmetic record, three usable records and a new version hash.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-revised-draft.png)

Check the new draft before publishing: three usable records and a changed content version. The earlier published version is kept.

4.  Publish this draft with a rationale describing the added case, then wait for **Published**.
5.  Reopen **Support response checks** from **Published datasets** and refresh. It now contains all three records and the revised version.

![Published revised Support response checks version with three usable records, including the arithmetic case.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-revised-published.png)

The revised version is Published with three records after refresh. The original two-record native version remained unchanged.

The catalog opens the current version. Earlier runs keep the version they selected.

If the new version shows **Needs review**, follow [publication recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#publication-recovery) for the same operation.

## 6\. Copy a Martian dataset

1.  Open a `martian:` dataset from **Published datasets**. It offers **Copy to my datasets** instead of **Edit**.

Your workspace’s available Martian packs can differ. The examples use synthetic teaching records, not a security benchmark.

![Read-only martian:documentation-versioning-pack with three records and Copy to my datasets.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-martian-source.png)

This synthetic Martian pack is read-only. Copy to my datasets creates an editable organization draft; your available packs may differ.

2.  Choose **Copy to my datasets**. The editable organization draft opens with the reserved `martian:` prefix removed from its name. Check its copied records before making changes.

![Editable documentation-versioning-pack organization copy with three usable records and Publish controls.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-martian-copy.png)

Copy removes the reserved prefix and opens an editable three-record draft. Publication is still required.

3.  Review the automatic validation summary, choose **Publish**, enter a rationale and confirm. Wait for **Published**.
4.  Reopen your copy from **Published datasets** and refresh. Confirm its records and organization ownership. Reopening the original Martian dataset still shows the read-only source.

![Published organization copy of the Martian teaching pack with three usable records and its own content version.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-copy-published.png)

The organization copy is Published and survives refresh. Its separate native identity preserves the original read-only Martian pack.

The copy has its own dataset identity and version once published. Your edits apply to the organization copy.

To copy failed records from a run or import them from an export, see [Turn failed results into regression cases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/regression-cases.md).

## More editing and import options

Edit, archive, delete, or import JSON and CSV

Choose **Add record** to enter **Record ID**, **Input**, **Expected output**, **Status** and optional metadata manually. Select a row’s **Edit** action and **Save record** to change an existing record. The record ID is fixed when editing. **Active** records can be used in runs; **Archived** records remain in the dataset but are excluded from execution.

This separate **Dataset editing practice** example starts with three records. A temporary record was added, edited and archived, leaving four records with three usable and one archived.

![Dataset editing practice with one archived temporary record and three usable records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/dataset-record-archived.png)

Archiving preserves the temporary record in this draft while excluding it from execution: four records, three usable and one archived.

To remove the temporary record, select only its checkbox, choose **Delete selected (1)**, inspect **Delete 1 record?**, then confirm **Delete**. Earlier published versions are kept.

![Delete 1 record confirmation for only the temporary archived draft record.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/dataset-delete-confirmation.png)

Review the selected record count before confirming removal from the draft.

After deletion, the draft returned to three usable records. One new CSV record and one new JSON-array record were then imported. Each preview showed one new record and zero updates; refresh retained five usable records after both imports.

![JSON import preview showing one new record, zero updates and five final records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/dataset-json-import-preview.png)

The second additional import previews one new JSON-array record. The native import and subsequent refresh retained five usable records.

JSON accepts a bare record array or an object containing `items`. CSV uses a header such as `id,input,expected_output,status`; optional metadata columns begin with `metadata.`. In JSON/JSONL, `metadata` must be an object. Use one expected-output spelling, `expected_output` or `expectedOutput`, per record.

## Failures and recovery

-   For a stale revision or “reload” error, refresh the draft and review intervening edits before retrying.
-   Duplicate IDs within one upload, unsupported fields or malformed files reject that upload. Correct the reported rows and preview again.
-   **Discard** removes unpublished draft work. Deleting draft records does not remove earlier published versions.

### Publication recovery

If publication becomes **Stalled** or **Needs review**, open **Datasets → Publish activity** as an owner/admin and find the original row in **Publish operations**. New runs remain paused until the operation finishes or is aborted.

![Publish activity showing an interrupted three-record revision beside the earlier published two-record version, with Resume and Abort actions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-publish-activity.png)

Open Publish activity to find the pending operation and resume it when its prerequisites are ready.

Choose **Resume**, enter a rationale and continue from the saved checkpoints. Leave the assertion that an interrupted creation was **never submitted** unchecked unless that has been independently proven. Ask your workspace administrator or support for help when native submission is uncertain.

Wait for Published

An accepted **Resume** queues recovery. Wait for **Published**, then reopen and refresh the dataset to verify its records. Keep the original operation while investigating an uncertain result; creating another publication does not resolve it.

**Abort** discards the unpublished version, keeps the current published version and makes its draft editable again.

Next, [run the dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) or [organize evaluation projects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/projects.md).

---

# Run your first evaluation

> Connect an approved HTTP agent, prepare a small published dataset, and inspect a retained evaluation result.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/first-run/)

Current beta console · owner/admin to prepare dataset; member+ to run; viewer can read

Run three synthetic requests through an approved agent and compare its answers with explicit expected outputs. At the end, you will have a saved evaluation with a result for each selected record, an execution status, and inspectable evidence.

An evaluation measures the behavior described by its dataset and scoring rules. It does not establish that an agent is secure against every attack. Use a red teaming assessment for adversarial testing.

## Before you start

-   Use a workspace where Evals setup shows **Ready**. Select the **Default** project for this tutorial. See [evaluation projects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/projects.md) if Default is unavailable.
-   Use **owner** or **admin** access to create and publish the example dataset yourself. A **member** can run an already published dataset; a **viewer** can inspect results.
-   [Register, validate and approve a stateless HTTP agent connection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md). Dataset Evals supports approved HTTP chat targets. MCP, browser and session-backed targets cannot run this tutorial.
-   If you need a complete teaching HTTP target, [run the callback adapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/http-adapter.md). Its deterministic callback recognizes the three questions below; public HTTPS hosting is an explicit prerequisite for hosted console calls.
-   Choose an agent that you are authorized to call. Each eligible record sends one target request; your target provider may charge for it.

If Evals shows a setup warning, use **Refresh setup** after your administrator has resolved it. Refreshing cannot provision missing access by itself. If setup is Ready but the project is unavailable or archived, select **Default** in the project toolbar or ask an owner/admin about the available projects; repeatedly refreshing setup does not restore an archived project.

## 1\. Prepare a small published dataset

Open **Evals → Datasets**, confirm the organization, then open **Project** in the toolbar above the page title and explicitly select **Default**. Leave Default selected through publication and the first run. Published datasets are shared across evaluation projects in your organization; the selected project determines where the new run belongs.

To make the example self-contained, save the following as `first-evaluation.jsonl`. These are simple instruction-following checks. For an agent intentionally restricted to another task, replace them with three reviewed examples of its intended behavior and corresponding exact answers.

```jsonl
{"id":"ready","input":"Reply with exactly READY and nothing else.","expected_output":"READY","status":"ACTIVE"}
{"id":"hello","input":"Reply with exactly HELLO and nothing else.","expected_output":"HELLO","status":"ACTIVE"}
{"id":"four","input":"What is 2 + 2? Reply with only the digit 4.","expected_output":"4","status":"ACTIVE"}
```

1.  Click **New dataset**, enter **First evaluation** in **Name**, and choose **Create draft**.
2.  Choose **Import file**. In **Import records**, use **File (up to 20 MiB)** to select the file, check that the preview reports **3 new** records, then click **Import**.
3.  Check that the draft shows **3 usable in runs** and no missing input or expected output.
4.  Click **Publish**, explain the reviewed example in **Rationale**, and confirm **Publish**. Wait for **Published**.
5.  Open **First evaluation** from the published dataset list and inspect the records. The [dataset guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md) explains each authoring and publication control.

![Published three-record First evaluation dataset reopened after a full page refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-dataset.png)

The published dataset retains READY, HELLO and 4 with all three records usable after refresh. Choose Use in eval to configure a run.

## 2\. Configure the run

1.  Confirm **Default** is selected in the project toolbar. On the published dataset, click **Use in eval**. This opens **Runs** with **Run an evaluation** and the dataset selected. You can also open **Runs → Run eval**.
2.  In **Agent**, choose your approved HTTP agent.
3.  In **Dataset**, confirm **First evaluation**.
4.  Leave **Target-call budget** at **Up to 100 active records**. This is a ceiling: the three-record dataset contains only three eligible requests. Selecting 100 does not manufacture another 97 records.
5.  Click **Start evaluation** once.

![Run an evaluation dialog with approved teaching HTTP agent, published three-record dataset and 100-record ceiling.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-form.png)

The three-record dataset is selected. Up to 100 active records is a ceiling; this run has only three eligible target requests.

## 3\. Follow execution

The run receives an `EV-` code and opens its detail view. The progress indicator reports how many records have finished. Requests execute sequentially, with one active target evaluation allowed per organization across its projects.

![EV-1001 actually running with zero records finished and cooperative stop available.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-progress.png)

The admitted run is Running. Wait for recorded results; Stop after current request cooperatively stops further work.

Wait for **Completed**. If you need to stop, use **Stop after current request** and follow the [stopping guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/stopping-and-recovery.md). A completed run can contain failed checks or request errors; completion does not mean every answer passed.

## 4\. Inspect and verify the saved result

1.  Read **Results** and its **Input**, **Expected**, **Actual output**, **Exact match** and **Latency** columns.
2.  Click **Inspect** on a record. Compare the actual answer with the expected answer and inspect **View trace** when a trace is available.
3.  Open **Evaluation provenance** to inspect the recorded dataset and run identity.
4.  Refresh the page and reopen the same `EV-` run. Confirm the result rows and terminal state remain available.

![EV-1001 completed with three passed responses and retained results after a page refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-results.png)

The Results tab shows the answer and exact-match verdict for each of the three example records.

Exact match ignores leading/trailing whitespace and letter case. Extra explanation or different punctuation can still fail. A failed check is useful evidence about this dataset; review the response before changing the expected answer.

## If something fails

-   **No runtime target** or unavailable agent: ask an owner/admin to complete connection validation and approval. Connection changes or revoked authorization require reapproval.
-   **An eval run is already in progress**: let the organization’s active run finish or stop it before launching another.
-   **Unknown dataset**, empty dataset or skipped records: reopen the published dataset and verify active records have usable input and expected output.
-   **Retry saved launch**: use that action to inspect the existing launch request after a lost acknowledgement. Do not create another run to work around uncertainty.

Next, [understand results and scores](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md), [compare two runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md), or [run evaluations from Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/evaluations.md).

---

# Collect human reviews

> Create typed review queues, answer required questions, verify completion and retain reviewer history.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/human-reviews/)

Current beta console · member+ reviews own/unassigned work; owner/admin assigns others

Collect attributed human ratings on saved evaluation responses. A queue defines which results need which questions; it becomes complete only after the required answers and their native feedback are verified. Human ratings remain separate from the original automated scores.

## Before you start

Use a **Completed** run in a writable project in the current beta console. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can create queues and review work assigned to them. Owners/admins can assign or reassign another reviewer’s work. The reviewer must be an active non-viewer member of the same organization. Viewers can read authorized review results without submitting answers.

Choose a small set of synthetic results for the first queue. Each queue accepts up to 100 selected results and one to eight distinct required questions. Creating and answering human reviews makes no target or model call.

## 1\. Create the review queue

1.  Open the completed run’s **Results** tab and select the records you want reviewed.
2.  Click **Create review queue**; the action includes the selected-record count.
3.  Enter **Queue name**.
4.  Define the first required question using **Criterion**, **Question** and **Answer type**. Use Boolean, numeric, categorical or text; set the applicable numeric bounds or category labels.
5.  Use **Add required question** for another criterion, or select **Reusable question** and choose **Add saved question**. A saved question is appended; remove the unused default question with **Remove question 1** if you want only the saved rubric.
6.  Confirm **Assign reviewer**. Keep yourself or an unassigned workflow unless you have administrator authority to assign another person.
7.  Click **Create queue**.

![Real queue form defining required questions for one selected teaching response.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-queue.png)

Create a small queue and define distinct required criteria. Additional question fields continue below the visible part of this real form.

Choose criterion names that clearly distinguish the questions. A result cannot silently join overlapping review chains that reuse a criterion with a conflicting queue/question schema.

## 2\. Answer a required question

1.  Click **Inspect** on a selected result.
2.  In **Human review**, choose the required **Review question**. Read its instruction alongside the input, expected output and actual answer.
3.  Set **Review rating**. For Boolean questions, choose **Pass** or **Fail**. For other types, choose **Complete** and enter **Numeric answer**, select **Category**, or write **Text answer**.
4.  Explain the rating in **Review explanation**. A completed answer needs an explanation and a value valid for that question.
5.  Click **Save review** and wait for the saved state. Repeat for every required question on every selected result.

![Member text answer and explanation saved for the READY evaluation item.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-answer.png)

The member saved a text answer with an evidence-based explanation. This capture still shows MLflow pending for that answer; verify native persistence and queue completion in the next step.

Use **Pending review** when the answer is not complete. Saving pending work does not satisfy the queue’s required question. Finish or resolve pending edits before moving to another result when the drawer shows **Review changes pending**.

## 3\. Verify queue completion

1.  Open **Evals → Reviews**.
2.  Select the queue in **Review queues**.
3.  Inspect **Review queue summary** and the number of answers verified. Wait for **Complete**; a local save notification alone is not native-feedback completion.
4.  Use **Review filter** to inspect completed reviews, and open a review to read the explanation and retained history.
5.  Refresh and reopen the queue. Confirm its answers, reviewer attribution and completion remain available.

![Completed review queue with four verified typed answers after a full page refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-complete.png)

Complete means all four latest answers are verified: text, category READY, numeric 5 and Boolean Pass. These persisted answers are attributed to the synthetic member account.

For two results with three required questions, six latest answers must be complete and verified. A newer answer supersedes the prior answer in the current view while the history remains attributable.

## 4\. Reuse a stable question definition

1.  From Reviews, click **Manage questions**.
2.  Choose **New review question**, define the criterion/question/answer type and relevant bounds/options, and save the question version.
3.  When creating another queue, select that version using **Reusable question → Add saved question**.
4.  To change the definition later, choose **Create next version**. Existing queues retain their original question versions.

![Reusable Boolean review question at immutable version two.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-questions.png)

Create next version saves a new question version. Existing queues keep the wording of their selected version.

Question versions let reviewers use the same rubric consistently. They do not cause existing completed answers to be rewritten.

## Blind review and agreement

In a workspace that supports blind double review, submit your own complete answer for a case and question before reading another reviewer’s answer. Other questions on the same case remain blind until you answer them.

With the Evals core from SDK 0.3.1, judge agreement, reviewer agreement and calibration reports use only answers the signed-in reader can see. Two reviewers can see different labelled counts until both have answered. A calibration re-check requires access to every item in the saved cohort. Ask your workspace administrator which review features your deployment supports. [SDK reference on blind review and calibration](https://github.com/MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/blob/v0.3.1/docs/evals.md#blind-double-review)

## Failures and recovery

-   For a stale review, reload the latest answer before editing; do not overwrite another reviewer’s work with an old revision.
-   If a save acknowledgement is delayed, wait and refresh the latest review before submitting another edit; another submission can create an additional history entry. Use **Retry saved review** after an unresolved acknowledgement. The same saved submission is inspected before another is admitted.
-   A non-admin cannot reassign work currently assigned to someone else. Ask an owner/admin to change the assignment.
-   If a saved answer shows **MLflow pending**, use **Sync saved feedback** to retry that retained assessment, then recheck the queue. Do not use **Save review** again merely to synchronize feedback.
-   A queue waiting for native feedback can show pending synchronization after local answers exist. **Reconcile native queue**, when offered, checks its recorded feedback. Preserve unresolved evidence for administrator review rather than marking it complete manually.
-   A rating is an attributed opinion under a rubric. It does not independently prove an exploit, permission boundary or business-side effect.

Next, [compare compatible scored runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) or [triage quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

---

# Score saved outputs and define judges

> Apply code criteria or versioned model rubrics to completed outputs with explicit cost and provenance controls.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/judging/)

Current beta console · member+ applies; owner/admin defines native judges

Add supplementary assessments to a completed evaluation without sending its prompts to the target again. Use code criteria for deterministic checks or a versioned model judge for an explicitly defined rubric. The original canonical exact-match results remain intact.

## Before you start

Use a **Completed** run in a writable project in the current beta console. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can apply scorers. Creating or versioning a custom judge requires **owner** or **admin** access.

Model judging additionally must be enabled in your organization’s environment and requires your explicit acknowledgement of provider charges. A disabled criterion labelled **Requires operator setup** cannot be enabled by acknowledging cost. Ask your administrator about availability. Reading or editing a judge definition does not itself invoke the model.

## 1\. Apply a code criterion

1.  Open **Evals → Runs** and select a completed run.
2.  Click **Score saved outputs**.
3.  Leave **Suite version** at **Ad hoc criteria**.
4.  Select the code criteria you need: **Exact match**, **Contains expected text**, **Valid JSON** or **Response length (characters)**.
5.  Click **Apply scorers** once and wait for the saved-output job to finish.

![Three saved-output code criteria selected, with model criteria unavailable.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-code.png)

Contains expected text, Valid JSON and Response length score retained answers. Model judges require provider setup.

Only the saved outputs are scored. **Valid JSON** is a syntax check, not your business schema. **Contains expected text** is a substring check, not semantic correctness. Response length counts Unicode characters. Choose criteria that actually measure the property you care about.

Inspect a result’s **Assessments** after the job completes. The teaching response `READY` contains its expected text and has five characters, while failing JSON syntax. Its original exact-match result still passes. The recorded native persistence state tells you whether the additional feedback has been retained.

![Persisted native code feedback for the saved READY response.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-code-feedback.png)

READY contains the expected text and has five characters, but is not valid JSON. All three code feedback entries show MLflow persisted; the original exact-match result still passes.

## 2\. Add built-in model opinions

1.  Open **Score saved outputs** on the completed run and leave **Suite version** at **Ad hoc criteria**.
2.  Clear criteria you do not want, then select **Correctness judge** and **Safety judge** when they are available.
3.  Read and select **I acknowledge that model judging can incur provider charges.**
4.  Click **Apply scorers** once. Reopen **Score saved outputs** to follow the job, then wait for its terminal state.
5.  Select the corresponding **Assessment job** and inspect a result’s **Assessments**. Read the value, explanation and **Model opinion** persistence state together.

![Available correctness and safety judges selected with provider-cost acknowledgement.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-model-judges-selection.png)

Select the correctness and safety judges and acknowledge provider charges before applying them.

The local teaching example produced six values across three saved responses, with zero judgment errors. Correctness and safety were both rated true for these benign examples. **Assessment identity** retained the model/judge revision; the original exact-match outcomes stayed unchanged. These ratings describe this small sample, not the target’s general security.

![Real correctness and safety model opinions with retained feedback and source identity.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-model-judges-feedback.png)

The saved READY result has true safety and correctness opinions, explanations and persisted MLflow feedback. Assessment identity records the Bedrock GLM-5 judge revision. One pending feedback delivery was reconciled without requesting another judgment.

If a saved value and explanation exist but their MLflow state is pending, use **Sync saved feedback** to reconcile that assessment’s delivery. Wait, refresh and reselect the original job. The action delivers the existing judgment.

## 3\. Define a custom model rubric

1.  As an owner/admin, open **Evals → Judges** and click **New judge**.
2.  Enter a stable **Judge name**, such as `answer_quality`, and a useful **Description**.
3.  Write **Instructions** describing what to judge from the saved input/output and expected value. For example:

```text
Assess whether {{ outputs }} answers {{ inputs }} with the required factual
content from {{ expectations }}. Return true only when the required answer is
present and the response does not contradict it. Explain the decision using
the saved text; do not assume external actions or unrecorded facts.
```

4.  Choose **Output type**: `boolean`, `numeric`, `categorical` or `text`. For numeric output, set **Minimum** and **Maximum**; for categorical output, enter one category per line in **Category options**.
5.  Click **Save version 1**. Reopen the judge and confirm the saved immutable version.

![Real Boolean custom-judge definition with a stable name and saved-text instructions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-definition.png)

Owner enters the docs\_answer\_present Boolean rubric before Save version 1. Saving the definition invokes no judging model.

A judge name begins with a lowercase letter and uses lowercase letters, digits or underscores. Keep the rubric specific and review it against examples before relying on its ratings. Saving a rubric does not establish judge accuracy.

## 4\. Apply a particular judge version

1.  Return to the completed run and open **Score saved outputs**.
2.  Under **Ad hoc criteria**, select the custom judge. Use the version selector beside it to choose the intended version, including a historical version if needed.
3.  If you choose **Policy compliance judge**, fill **Policy guidelines**.
4.  Read and select **I acknowledge that model judging can incur provider charges.**
5.  Click **Apply scorers** and wait for the job’s terminal state.
6.  Select that **Assessment job**, inspect a result’s **Assessments**, and check its typed value, rationale and persistence state. Refresh and verify the same job and feedback remain recorded.

### Create and apply v2

For the pictured differences, use the completed [comparison-variant run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) with the saved outputs `ready`, `hello` and `4.`. Your own responses can receive identical opinions when both rubrics accept them.

1.  Open **Evals → Judges**, find the same judge, and choose **Create next version**.
2.  Edit **Description** and **Instructions**. In this example, v2 requires the expected letter case and punctuation; v1 accepts the required answer despite those differences.
3.  Click **Save version 2**. Reopen the judge to read **Version history** and confirm that both definitions remain available. Saving v2 does not apply it to a run.

![Create version 2 preserves the judge name while allowing stricter instructions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-next-version.png)

The immutable judge name remains disabled. Owner prepares a stricter Boolean v2 rubric requiring expected case and punctuation, then saves it as a new version.

![Read-back version history retaining the stricter v2 and original v1 definitions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-version-history.png)

The real Version history panel retains both Boolean definitions, their original instructions and capture-time creation dates. Saving v2 did not replace v1.

4.  Return to the same completed run and open **Score saved outputs**. Under **Ad hoc criteria**, select the custom judge and choose **v2** in its adjacent version selector.
5.  Read and select **I acknowledge that model judging can incur provider charges.** Then click **Apply scorers** once.
6.  Wait for the new job to finish, select its **Assessment job**, and inspect the retained **Assessments**. Refresh and reselect that job to verify persistence.

![Two persisted opinions on the same punctuation response with different retained definition identities.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-feedback.png)

Compare the feedback and rationale for each rubric version alongside its recorded judge definition.

The recorded v1 and v2 jobs produced three true and three false opinions on the same saved responses. Those ratings reflect different instructions. The target’s two canonical passes and one failure stayed unchanged; existing jobs retained their original rubric version.

### Use a historical version

The catalogue checkbox label names the latest version. Use the adjacent version selector to pin an older one; the historical v1 remains selectable after v2 exists.

To score another completed run with that older rubric, repeat the application steps at the start of this section, selecting **v1** before cost acknowledgement and **Apply scorers**. To inspect an existing v1 result, reselect its saved **Assessment job**.

![Latest catalogue label v2 with historical v1 selected for execution.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-historical-version.png)

The checkbox label identifies the latest catalogue version; the adjacent selector pins v1. This actual selection was admitted against baseline EV-1001 after v2 existed and retained three native v1 assessments.

For a retained version record, select the relevant **Assessment job**, use **Results → Export JSON**, and inspect `assessments[].provenance["martian.native_scorer_version"]`. **Assessment identity** shows the job, definition digest and runtime source. A source suffix such as `martian-eval-judge-v2` is the judging engine’s revision; it is separate from your rubric’s version number.

## Interpret and recover

Boolean results can form pass rates; numeric, category and text outputs retain their own types. Coverage and errors matter alongside scores. A model opinion is separate from a verified security finding or independently observed business outcome.

Ad hoc judgments do not automatically define a passing gate. **Unconfigured** means no threshold policy was supplied, even if every Boolean rating is true. For built-in criteria, a [scoring suite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md) can supply a threshold and minimum coverage. Registered custom rubrics cannot be attached to suite versions in the current console; their jobs have no suite-threshold control. Review their typed values and coverage directly.

A scoring request supports one to seven unique criteria. One active scoring job is allowed per organization. Completed runs are required. If submission is unresolved, use **Retry saved scoring request** to inspect that same operation. Stop controls are cooperative and may allow the in-flight judgment to finish; see [stopping and recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/stopping-and-recovery.md).

If feedback delivery remains uncertain, retain the run and job identifiers for administrator review rather than rerunning paid work. Applying a different job or rubric does not overwrite the first job’s provenance.

Next, [apply a reusable suite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md) or [collect human reviews](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md).

---

# Read the Evals dashboard

> Interpret project trace volume, errors, latency, recorded usage and typed quality summaries without rerunning a target.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/overview/)

Current beta console · Any customer role

Use the project dashboard to understand the native traces retained for your selected scope. It summarizes recorded activity; it does not launch an evaluation or schedule model calls.

## Before you start

Any customer role can read authorized evidence. Choose a ready Evals project with retained native traces. This is **Evals → Overview**, distinct from an individual evaluation run’s Overview tab and from saved-score Monitoring.

The screenshots use the two retained requests from the [native conversation walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md#3-group-recorded-conversations). You can use any authorized traces in your selected project; opening this dashboard does not call the agent again.

## 1\. Choose the trace selection

1.  Open **Evals → Overview** and confirm the organization and **Project**.
2.  Use **Search trace content**, **Trace state** and **Trace order** to select the activity you need.
3.  Open **Filters** (accessible name **More filters**) for session, user, time, latency or assessment criteria.
4.  Choose **Apply filters**. Read the applied scope and incomplete-coverage notice before interpreting totals. **Refresh overview** rereads the selection.

![Real Evals project dashboard with two requests, zero errors, latency metrics and unavailable recorded usage.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-project-overview.png)

The two retained HTTP traces are included. The dashboard reports zero execution errors, P50 41 ms and P95 67 ms; usage remains unavailable.

## 2\. Read performance and usage

| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Requests | Matching recorded native traces, rather than a count of every provider call or evaluation case |
| Error rate | The share with recorded ERROR trace state; a failed quality check is a separate result |
| P50 / P95 latency | Percentiles of reported trace durations |
| Trace volume | Recorded activity over time; it is not a future execution schedule |
| Total tokens / Total cost (USD) | Reported usage in the matching traces, accompanied by reporting coverage |

1.  In **Recorded usage**, check how many traces reported tokens and cost.
2.  Treat missing reports as unavailable. No reported bill is not an independently established zero bill; partial coverage is not total provider spend.
3.  Check the selected time window and coverage again before comparing two selections.

![Recorded usage showing zero reporting coverage beside Boolean, numeric and categorical feedback summaries.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-overview-recorded-usage.png)

Neither trace reports tokens or cost. Three saved feedback definitions produce their own typed summaries; the separate expectation is excluded.

## 3\. Interpret Quality summary

1.  Read **Assessment**, **Type**, **Recorded values** and **Result** together.
2.  Boolean feedback can show pass rates. Numeric feedback can show means. Categorical/text values retain their recorded-value counts rather than becoming pass percentages.
3.  [Inspect the underlying traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) when a summary needs explanation. Use [native annotations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/trace-annotations.md) when you intend to add a human opinion or expectation.

For example, feedback named `response_correct` appears as **response correct**. A single Pass gives **100% pass** for that one recorded judgment; a numeric rating of `4.5` gives **Mean 4.5**. Text feedback appears as **Categorical**, with the text and its count. These examples describe the saved opinions, rather than independently verifying the response.

These are native feedback aggregates. They do not replace canonical exact-match results, a versioned suite gate or verified security outcomes. For gate history, choose **Monitoring** and follow [suites and monitoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md).

## Failures and limits

-   Aggregates inspect at most 1,000 matching traces. Narrow the selection when coverage is incomplete; do not describe a bounded sample as all history.
-   After a read error, use **Refresh overview** and retain the scope/error if it persists. Reading the dashboard does not repair missing instrumentation.
-   An empty selection can mean missing telemetry or restrictive filters. It does not establish that the application made no requests.

Continue with [trace inspection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) or [individual run results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md).

---

# Organize evaluation projects

> Select, create and archive projects while preserving organization boundaries and historical evaluation evidence.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/projects/)

Current beta console · owner/admin creates/archives; all customer roles browse

Use projects to group evaluation runs, traces, judge definitions and review work inside your organization. The project selector determines the context for the Evals page you are viewing. Published datasets are shared across the organization’s projects.

## Before you start

Use an organization with ready Evals setup in the current beta console. Any customer role can browse authorized projects. Creating or archiving a project requires **owner** or **admin** access. A project is an evaluation grouping, not another organization or a permission grant to a different tenant.

To verify run history in the new project, have an approved agent and a small published dataset ready. Complete the setup in [your first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) if these are missing.

## 1\. Select a project

1.  Open **Evals** and locate the organization/project toolbar above the page title.
2.  Check the organization name and your role.
3.  Open **Project** and choose **Default** or a named ready project.
4.  Move between **Runs**, **Traces** and other Evals sections. The selected project remains part of that navigation.

![Default project selected above the real retained run list.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-projects-selector.png)

Use the Project picker to switch between the Default project and a separate evaluation project.

Runs and trace views are project scoped. Datasets remain available across projects in the same organization. Selecting another project does not copy datasets or give you access to another organization.

## 2\. Create a project

1.  As an owner/admin, click **New project**.
2.  In **New evaluation project**, enter a **Name** and optional **Description** that describe the evaluation work.
3.  Click **Create project** once.
4.  Wait for the new project to appear selected in the toolbar. Open **Runs** to begin work in it.

![New evaluation project form with a synthetic name and description.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-projects-create.png)

Enter a name and description, then create the project once. This capture is the reviewed form before submission; the actual request created a ready project.

Creating a project establishes its evaluation context; it does not call an agent or run a model judge. If setup returns an unresolved response, use **Retry project setup** to inspect the saved setup request rather than creating an identically named replacement.

## 3\. Verify retained scope

1.  Refresh the page and confirm the named project is still selected.
2.  If the project is empty, click **Run eval** and follow [Configure the run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md#2-configure-the-run), keeping your new project selected instead of Default. Use the approved agent and small published dataset prepared above, then wait for the admitted run to finish.
3.  Open that run and confirm its run code and dataset identity.
4.  Change to **Default** and check that the project-specific run list changes.
5.  Return to the named project and confirm its saved work remains available.

An empty project list can reflect unavailable Evals setup, not an absence of permission to the whole console. Use **Refresh setup** after the underlying issue has been resolved. A URL naming an unavailable project is not sufficient to grant access.

## 4\. Archive a finished project

Archiving is an administrative terminal state in the current console: there is no restore interface. Use it only when the team is finished admitting new work to that project.

1.  Select a custom ready project. The Default context does not expose the same archive action.
2.  Wait for its active target evaluation or scoring work to finish.
3.  Choose the toolbar’s **Archive project** action.
4.  Read **Archive project?** and confirm **Archive project**.
5.  Verify the archived-project warning and refresh. Historical runs and traces remain readable, while new evaluation work is disabled for that project.

![Archived Teaching regressions project retains completed EV-1005 and disables Run eval.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-projects-archive.png)

After archiving and a full refresh, the historical run remains readable and Run eval is disabled. The example retains a changed-callback run with two passes and one failure; archiving does not rescore it. There is no restore interface.

## Failures and limits

-   A project whose state is not ready cannot admit new evaluation work.
-   Active target or scoring jobs can prevent archiving. Let them finish or use their documented cooperative stop controls before retrying.
-   Archiving does not delete historical evidence or revoke an agent connection. Manage connections through [Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md).
-   Organization-wide concurrency still applies across projects: creating projects does not create extra target-run capacity.

Next, [run an evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) or [inspect traces and sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md).

---

# Investigate quality issues

> Find recorded execution errors and failed Boolean assessments, inspect their evidence, and retain attributed triage decisions.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/quality-issues/)

Current beta console · all customer roles browse; member+ triages

Turn a recorded failure signal into an inspectable triage decision. Quality issues group execution errors and explicit failed Boolean assessments from the current trace selection. They help direct investigation; they are separate from verified red teaming findings.

## Before you start

Use the current beta console with retained Evals trace evidence in the selected project. Any customer role can inspect authorized issue groups. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can triage in a writable project.
