To exercise a positive example, use a real saved run containing a failed Boolean criterion or recorded execution error. Do not edit a screenshot or fabricate an error to demonstrate a group. An empty issue view is a valid result when the selected evidence contains no supported failure signals.

For a free teaching example, apply the code criteria from [saved-output scoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/judging.md#1-apply-a-code-criterion) to the first-run dataset. Plain `READY` and `HELLO` fail JSON syntax while passing exact match. This demonstrates a criterion mismatch to investigate; choose criteria that fit your real task’s requirements.

## 1\. Find the issue selection

1.  Open **Evals → Quality issues** and confirm the project.
2.  Use **Search trace content**, state/time filters and **Apply filters** to select the relevant requests.
3.  Read the coverage note. Choose an **Issue groups** entry to see its recorded examples and open count.
4.  If a group says it shows only some examples, narrow the search to inspect the relevant subset.

![Actual failed exact-match and JSON Boolean groups are found across eleven retained traces.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-issues-groups.png)

The candidate output is \[4.\] and the expected answer is \[4\]. The trace executed OK; its Boolean quality assessment failed. Numeric gate failures are not automatically Boolean issue groups.

Numeric, categorical and text feedback retains its type and evaluation policy. A low-looking number or a category named “poor” is not automatically converted into an explicit Boolean failure. The issue list does not establish all possible quality problems in the agent.

## 2\. Inspect evidence before changing status

1.  On a group’s row, choose **Inspect trace**.
2.  Inspect the saved input/output, execution state and relevant assessment or error in **Trace details**.
3.  Check the definition and recorded rationale where available. Determine whether this is a target error, a rubric disagreement, missing evidence or another concrete problem.
4.  Close the inspector to return to the same group and filters.

Keep the evidence distinct from your interpretation. An error trace does not by itself establish a successful attack or a production-side business effect.

## 3\. Record a triage decision

1.  Select the relevant trace checkboxes, up to 100 traces per triage request.
2.  Click **Triage N selected**.
3.  In **Status**, choose **open**, **investigating**, **resolved** or **dismissed**, as appropriate.
4.  Enter a clear **Rationale**: what you observed, your decision, and any follow-up or external fix reference.
5.  Click **Save triage**.

![Triage form selects investigating and records a concrete punctuation-regression rationale.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-issues-triage.png)

Record the observed difference and an appropriate status before saving. This form concerns retained teaching evidence, not a verified security finding or a deployment fix.

The decision records your signed-in identity, rationale and time with the selected traces. A triage status does not rerun the agent, change an expected output, repair a deployment or erase the underlying assessment.

## 4\. Verify the decision remains recorded

1.  Read the updated triage value in the group table.
2.  Refresh **Quality issues**, reapply the same filters if needed, and reopen the affected group.
3.  Confirm the selected traces retain the intended status.
4.  If a remediation changed the agent, execute a separately authorized new evaluation and [compare it with the baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md). Resolving a triage item is not evidence that the fix passed.

![The exact-match issue retains Investigating after a full refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-issues-retained.png)

The refreshed selection retains Investigating for the same trace. Native readback also retained the account, rationale and timestamp; triage did not change the saved output.

## Failures and limits

-   **No quality issues in this search** means no recorded execution errors or explicit failed Boolean assessments were found in that bounded selection. It is not a security certificate or a guarantee about unexamined traces.
-   An unavailable/foreign trace cannot be triaged by guessing its ID. Confirm the organization and project.
-   Archived projects retain readable evidence while rejecting new triage work.
-   Aggregates inspect up to 1,000 matching traces. Narrow filters when coverage is incomplete; a visible group count and its displayed examples can have different bounds.
-   If the save fails, retain the intended selection/rationale, inspect the reported error and refresh the current evidence before retrying. Do not repeatedly submit different decisions to force a visible state.

Next, [retain a useful trace view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) or [collect a human rubric review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md).

---

# Turn failed results into regression cases

> Copy a saved failure into an editable dataset draft, or import its exported records while preserving the correct expected answer.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/regression-cases/)

Current beta console · Member, admin or owner; observed Owner walkthrough

Save a failed record as a test case that can catch the same problem in a later evaluation. Finish with an editable draft containing the reviewed input, expected answer and source-run metadata. Creating the draft uses saved results; it does not repeat the target call.

## Before you start

Use a **Member**, **Admin** or **Owner** account in a ready Evals organization. Start with a completed run containing a failed record, such as the [changed-answer comparison example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md).

In this example, the expected output is `4` and the agent replied `4.`. Keep the correct answer `4` as the expected output.

Choose one path per case. Direct copying and file export use different record IDs, so combining both in the same draft can add duplicate questions.

## Copy the selected result directly

1.  Open **Evals → Runs**, select the completed run and stay on **Results**. Read the canonical **Exact match** column separately from supplementary **Assessments**.
2.  Select the failed row’s checkbox. Confirm **1 result selected**. Select at most 100 records for one dataset action.

![One canonical failed EV-1003 record selected, expected 4 and actual 4.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-selection.png)

Select only the canonical failed row. One result is selected; saved-result authoring remains available while a separate publication pauses new runs.

3.  Click **Add selected to dataset (1)**. Under **Draft**, choose **New draft…** and enter **Regression cases from EV-1003**. Keep **Expected output → Keep the run’s expected output**.

![Add one saved result to a new draft while keeping the original expected output.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-dialog.png)

Choose New draft and Keep the run's expected output. The correct answer stays 4; the failing answer 4. is not accepted as ground truth.

4.  Click **Add to draft** once. After the success message, open **Datasets → Drafts** and select the new draft. The dataset page opens on published datasets by default.
5.  Check the input, expected output and usable count. Refresh and confirm the same record remains. In this example, the expected output is `4`.

![Refreshed Regression cases from EV-1003 draft with one usable record and expected output 4.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-draft.png)

The direct-copy draft retained revision 2 and one usable record after refresh. Its source-run/result metadata was inspected without another save.

The **Edit** dialog shows metadata linking the record to its source run and result. Cancel if you only wanted to inspect it. Choose **Use the agent’s actual output** only after a reviewer confirms that answer is correct.

## Alternative: import an exported failure

Use a separate empty draft for this alternative.

1.  In the original run, select the failed row and click **Export selected failures (1)**. The downloaded `EV-1003-regression-cases.json` contains `source_run_id`, `dataset_id` and an `items` array.

The complete export is not an import-ready dataset. Importing it directly produces **JSON datasets accept only name, description and items**; the preview is rejected and **Import** stays disabled.

![Import preview rejecting the complete failure-export wrapper and disabling Import.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-wrapper-error.png)

The export's top-level provenance fields are not accepted by dataset import. This real rejected dry run changed no records.

2.  Save only the `items` array as a new JSON file, preserving each record’s values and metadata. For example, run this Python 3 command in the download folder, replacing the input filename if needed:

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path

export = json.loads(Path("EV-1003-regression-cases.json").read_text())
Path("selected-failure-import-ev1003.json").write_text(
    json.dumps(export["items"], indent=2) + "\n"
)
PY
```

3.  Open **Evals → Datasets → New dataset**. Name it **Imported failure from EV-1003**, then choose **Create draft**.
4.  Choose **Import file** and select the new JSON array. For the empty draft in this example, the preview shows **1 new · 0 updated · 1 records after import**.

![Corrected items-array import preview in a separate empty draft, showing one new record.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-array-preview.png)

The extracted items array previews one new record, zero updates and one final record. The draft behind the preview is still empty until Import.

5.  Click **Import** once. Refresh and confirm one usable record with expected output `4`. Its metadata retains the observed output `4.` and source identifiers.

![Refreshed Imported failure from EV-1003 draft with one usable record and expected output 4.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-imported.png)

The separate file-import draft retained one usable record after one Import and refresh. Metadata preserves the source run/result and the observed answer, including its trailing period.

## Verify and continue

Both paths retained one usable record after refresh in their separate drafts. Neither changed the original run or published dataset. Review and [publish the draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#4-publish-and-verify-the-version) before using it in a new evaluation.

-   If creating a draft succeeds but adding the result fails, reuse that confirmed draft during recovery; another new draft can leave extra copies.
-   Import updates match IDs, rather than matching prompts. Inspect the new/updated counts before merging files into an existing draft.
-   A saved case does not establish that a later target has been fixed. [Run the published dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) to measure that.

---

# Understand results and scores

> Inspect record-level outputs, exact-match results, supplementary assessments, exports and evaluation provenance.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/results-and-scores/)

Current beta console · all customer roles read/export; member+ for supplementary mutations

Read a saved evaluation from its overall execution state down to an individual input, answer and assessment. You will be able to distinguish a failed quality check from a failed request, retain exports, and explain which evidence supports a score.

## Before you start

Any customer role can inspect authorized saved runs in the current beta console. Complete a [first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) and confirm the correct project. Applying additional scoring or changing human reviews requires **member** access or higher; this guide’s read/export steps do not send new target requests.

## 1\. Open and filter a run

1.  Open **Evals → Runs** and select an `EV-` run code. Use **Search evaluation runs** and paging if necessary.
2.  Read the execution state and record counters. **Completed** means execution finished; it does not mean that every answer passed.
3.  On **Results**, use **Search results**, **Result status** or **Sort results** to find a record.
4.  Adjust **Rows** to page through results. Read **Input**, **Expected**, **Actual output**, **Exact match** and **Latency**.

![Completed evaluation result table showing three expected and actual answers, scores and latencies.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-results.png)

Completed is the execution state. Inspect each expected and actual answer and its score; this synthetic example has three passes.

| Record result | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Passed | The recorded response satisfied canonical exact match. |
| Failed | A response was recorded but did not match the expected answer. |
| Error | The request or processing path reported an error; read the saved error. |
| Skipped | The selected record was not executed or scored, for example after a cooperative stop or because it was unusable. |
| Pending | A result has not finished yet. |

Exact match compares the response and expected string after trimming outer whitespace and ignoring case. It does not ignore punctuation, remove an explanation, or establish semantic equivalence.

## 2\. Inspect a record

1.  Click **Inspect** on a result.
2.  In **Result and review**, compare the input, expected output and actual output.
3.  Read **Assessments** for any saved code-rule, model or human ratings. Each can retain its rationale, definition identity and persistence state.
4.  Use **View trace** for available execution evidence. **Previous result** and **Next result** let you inspect adjacent filtered results.

![Evaluation item inspector showing READY input, expected and actual output, latency and separate human review.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-results-inspector.png)

Inspect opens one retained record. Human review and supplementary assessments are separate from its original exact-match result.

Save or resolve an edited human review before navigating away when the drawer reports **Review changes pending**. Read [human reviews](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md) before assigning ratings.

## 3\. Interpret supplementary scores

For project-wide trace volume, latency, recorded usage and typed quality aggregates, use the separate [Evals dashboard guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/overview.md). The run-level Overview below describes this evaluation’s saved assessment jobs.

Open the run’s **Overview** and choose the relevant **Assessment job**. Supplementary criteria do not replace the original exact-match result:

-   **Contains expected text** checks a case-insensitive expected substring.
-   **Valid JSON** checks that the saved output parses as supported JSON; it does not check your application’s domain schema.
-   **Response length (characters)** reports Unicode character count.
-   Model judges and human ratings record opinions or rubric results with their own source and definition.

Boolean criteria can show pass rates and coverage. Numeric criteria retain numeric summaries; categorical and text values are not converted into a Boolean pass rate. A missing assessment is not a passing value. See [saved-output judging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/judging.md) and [suites and quality gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md).

![Original passing result alongside three separate persisted code assessments.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-code-feedback.png)

Supplementary code assessments do not replace canonical exact match. A JSON-syntax failure and a passing exact-match answer can both be correct under their different definitions.

## 4\. Inspect provenance and export

1.  Open **Evaluation provenance** and inspect the recorded run, dataset and available target/artifact identity.
2.  Return to **Results**, apply the filters you want to retain, and select **Export CSV** or **Export JSON**.
3.  Check the downloaded records against the visible selection. The result export follows the displayed filters; a small filtered export is not a complete-run export.
4.  Refresh and reopen the same run to confirm its results and assessment job remain available.

![Evaluation provenance with native FINISHED state, pinned dataset hash and unreported model and prompt versions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-results-provenance.png)

Native FINISHED and three passed metrics were read back. The dataset hash matches publication; absent agent, model and prompt revisions remain Not reported.

Dataset versions and declared artifact revisions describe what was recorded at admission. Unreported model or prompt versions remain unavailable. An agent name is not proof of a specific deployed model or prompt revision.

## Failures and limits

-   **MLflow telemetry needs administrator review** means native evidence may be incomplete even when local results exist. Retain the run code and ask your administrator to investigate; do not rerun the target merely to repair telemetry.
-   **Sync saved feedback** retries delivery of an existing assessment. It does not justify inventing a missing value or treating an uncertain write as persisted.
-   Latency and token/cost data describe recorded values. Missing usage is not zero usage and is not an independently verified bill.
-   Quality scores, human opinions and model opinions are separate from verified adversarial findings.

Next, [compare runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) or [inspect native traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md).

---

# Stop runs and recover uncertain work

> Stop target evaluations or saved-output scoring cooperatively, preserve retained evidence, and resolve uncertain submissions safely.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/stopping-and-recovery/)

Current beta console · member+ stops; all customer roles inspect retained work

Request a bounded stop without discarding results that have already arrived, and distinguish an unresolved acknowledgement from a new launch. This guide covers customer controls in the current beta console; it does not require internal worker, database or MLflow administration.

## Before you start

**Members**, **admins** and **owners** can request stops for authorized work. A **viewer** can inspect status and retained evidence. A target run must still be queued or running; scoring must still have an active job.

Use a deliberately bounded, authorized example when learning the controls. A stop is cooperative: a target request or model judgment already admitted can finish and may incur its normal charge. Stop is not a way to revoke an already sent request or undo external side effects.

For optional practice with the [HTTP teaching adapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/http-adapter.md), the [example README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/http-agent/README.md) includes `slow_agent:answer`, a callback that waits ten seconds. Confirm deadline headroom with your administrator before using it. Keep the three-record dataset and stop after at least one record finishes.

## 1\. Stop a target evaluation

1.  Open **Evals → Runs** in the active run’s project.
2.  Locate its `EV-` progress row and finished-record count.
3.  Click **Stop after current request** once.
4.  Observe **Stopping after the current request**. Wait for the in-flight request and finalization to finish.

![Real stopping intent with one completed record and another response pending.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-request-positive.png)

EV-1007 shows Stopping after the current request after the first record passed. The next response is still pending; acknowledgement alone is not terminal completion.

A queued run may stop before sending any request. An active run retains the current response and skips the selected records that have not been started. Other projects share the same organization-wide target-run admission limit.

## 2\. Verify the cancelled result

1.  Open the run detail and wait for **Cancelled**.
2.  Inspect retained responses and **Skipped** rows. Do not count skipped records as passing checks.
3.  Open **Evaluation provenance** and inspect the native run state when available; a verified cancelled native run is recorded as **KILLED**. A queued stop can finish before a native run exists.
4.  Refresh and reopen the same run. Confirm its terminal state and retained rows remain available.

![Cancelled evaluation retaining two passing responses and one skipped record.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-cancelled.png)

After refresh, the same cancelled run retains READY/HELLO responses, two passes, zero errors and one unstarted skipped record. Two requests reached the actual teaching target.

In the example, one record finished before the stop was requested. A second response finished while cancellation was pending, leaving **2 Passed, 0 Errors, 1 Skipped** and a native state of **KILLED**.

![Verified native KILLED provenance and matching two-pass, one-skipped metrics.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-native-killed.png)

Native provenance independently reads KILLED for this retained cancelled run, with two passed, zero failed, one skipped and zero errored metrics. The callback revision is explicitly customer-declared.

A cancellation acknowledgement is intent to stop, not proof that all physical work has ended. Wait for the terminal run state and relevant evidence before launching another evaluation. If the run has already finished, the UI/API can reject a late stop and keep its recorded result.

A cancelled run can retain target errors. Read the saved rows and any telemetry warning to see which requests succeeded.

## 3\. Stop saved-output scoring

1.  Open the completed target run and its **Score saved outputs** dialog. After **Apply scorers** admits a job, the dialog closes; reopen **Score saved outputs** while that job is still active.
2.  While a scoring job is active, click **Stop scoring after current judgment**.
3.  Observe **Stopping after the current judgment** and wait for the job to finish stopping.
4.  Inspect the selected **Assessment job** and the assessments already retained. Refresh and confirm the same job state and saved feedback.

![Real code-scoring job with Stopping after the current judgment and eight of twelve assessments scored.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-scoring.png)

The stop was acknowledged while eight of twelve code assessments had been produced. The configuration stays disabled while stopping. A separate local setup warning was visible behind the dialog; the retained source run remained Completed.

This stops supplementary scoring, not the target run that already completed. The in-flight judgment can finish; retained assessments are preserved, and unscored results remain missing. Partial coverage must not be interpreted as a passing full-run gate.

In the recorded code-only example, four criteria were selected for three saved responses. The stop was accepted at **8/12 scored**. The same cancelled job retained eight native assessments after refresh, with **2 of 3 evaluated** for each criterion and one missing value. The original target run still had three canonical passes. Here, “scored” counts assessments, including failing Boolean values; it does not count passing records.

![Cancelled scoring job retains two-thirds coverage while the source run keeps three canonical passes.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-scorecard.png)

After refresh and explicit selection of the cancelled job, each of four criteria shows two of three records evaluated and one missing value. All eight retained assessments had native IDs; the original target run still had three canonical passes.

## 4\. Resolve an uncertain acknowledgement

A network failure can occur after the service accepted a request but before the browser received its response. Use the action tied to the saved request:

| Screen | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Target-run launch | **Retry saved launch** |
| Saved-output scoring | **Retry saved scoring request** |
| Human answer | **Retry saved review** |
| Suite/queue mutation | **Retry saved request**, when offered |
| Project creation | **Retry project setup**, when offered |

Keep the original configuration while reconciling. These actions reuse the saved request identity to inspect/admit the same operation; they are not a request to run the target or paid model repeatedly until it passes. A request identity cannot be reused with different content.

## 5\. Handle setup, publication or telemetry failures

-   **Dataset updates are in progress**: new runs are paused while publication completes. Existing admitted runs may finish. An owner/admin can inspect **Datasets → Publish activity** for a stalled operation; use the [dataset recovery guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#failures-and-recovery).
-   **Refresh setup**: refreshes the readiness read after the underlying problem is resolved. It cannot authorize an unapproved connection or create missing model access.
-   Saved results with telemetry errors need administrator review. Retain the run/job code and error, rather than deleting evidence or rerunning the target to repair export.
-   A rotated, changed, expired or revoked agent connection can stop later target calls. Revalidate/approve through [Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md) before admitting new work.

If uncertainty remains after refreshing and reconciling the saved request, give your administrator the run code, job identity, time and displayed error. Avoid including tokens, passwords or unneeded response content in support messages.

Next, [inspect retained results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md) or [start another bounded evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) once the organization is ready for new work.

---

# Use scoring suites and monitoring

> Save immutable scoring criteria and thresholds, apply an exact suite version, and inspect retained quality-gate history.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/suites-and-monitoring/)

Current beta console · member+ versions/applies suites; all customer roles read monitoring

Save criteria and quality thresholds as a reusable suite, apply a particular version to completed outputs, and monitor its retained jobs and gate outcomes. This keeps a quality policy consistent across runs instead of rebuilding it differently each time.

## Before you start

Use your organization in the current beta console. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can create/version suites and apply them to completed runs. Any customer role can inspect authorized monitoring history. Have a completed evaluation in a writable project and understand the [meaning of its scores](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md).

Saving a suite makes no model calls. Applying code criteria uses saved outputs. Applying model criteria additionally needs enabled model judging and explicit cost acknowledgement. Custom registered judges are applied separately from these built-in-criterion suite definitions.

## 1\. Create a small code-scoring suite

1.  Open **Evals → Judges**, then choose **Scoring suites**.
2.  In **Suite definition**, choose **New suite** if another version is selected.
3.  Enter **Suite name**, for example **Response format checks**.
4.  Select **Contains expected text** and **Response length (characters)**.
5.  For `contains_expected`, set **Quality threshold** to `1`, **Better when** to **Higher**, and **Minimum coverage** to `1`.
6.  For `response_length`, choose a ceiling for the **mean character count**, set **Better when** to **Lower**, and keep **Minimum coverage** at `1`. For the short answers in the first-run tutorial, an example mean ceiling is `80`.
7.  Click **Create suite** and confirm that version 1 is selected.

![Saved code-only suite version1 with explicit pass-rate, mean-length and full-coverage thresholds.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-definition.png)

Response format checks v1 pins containment at 1 and mean response length at most 80 characters, with full coverage. Saving this definition makes no model calls.

A Boolean threshold is a pass rate from `0` to `1`. A response-length threshold compares the **mean** across evaluated records; it is not a maximum allowed for every response. Inspect the range and individual results when outliers matter. Minimum coverage is also `0` to `1`; full coverage prevents missing/error assessments from being treated as satisfactory evidence. A blank threshold means that criterion has no configured gate; it is not an implicit passing gate.

## 2\. Apply an exact suite version

1.  Open a completed run and choose **Score saved outputs**.
2.  In **Suite version**, select **Response format checks · v1**.
3.  Confirm the pinned criteria and any policy instructions. Their controls are locked to the suite definition.
4.  If the chosen suite includes model criteria, read and select the provider-charge acknowledgement. The example code-only suite does not require a model call.
5.  Click **Apply scorers** and wait for completion.
6.  Select the resulting **Assessment job** and open the run’s **Overview** to inspect its scorecard, thresholds, coverage and gate results.

![Saved-output scoring dialog selects Response format checks v1 and locks its two code criteria.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-apply.png)

Select the exact suite version before applying it. The pinned code criteria are locked; this job scores saved responses without calling the teaching target again.

![Version1 code-suite scorecard passes both gates with three of three records evaluated.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-scorecard.png)

The completed v1 job has full coverage and no missing or error scores. Its response-length gate compares a mean of 3.67 with the ceiling of 80; the recorded range is 1–5.

A gate can be **Passed**, **Failed**, **Insufficient coverage** or **Unconfigured**. Job completion and gate success are different: a finished job may show a failed or unconfigured gate. Review the actual values and coverage before acting on the summary.

## 3\. Create a new version without changing history

1.  Return to **Scoring suites** and choose the prior version in **Edit suite version**.
2.  Change the relevant criteria, instructions or thresholds. For this teaching example, lower `response_length` from `80` to `3`, retaining its **Lower** direction and full coverage.
3.  Click **Save version 2**.
4.  Repeat [Apply an exact suite version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md#2-apply-an-exact-suite-version), selecting **Response format checks · v2** on the **same completed run**. Wait for the new scoring job to finish and inspect its **Overview**.

In the teaching example, version 2 lowers the mean response-length ceiling from `80` to `3`. The same three saved answers have mean length about `3.67`, so this newer gate fails while their canonical exact-match results remain passed. The earlier version 1 job still retains its passing `80`\-character policy.

![Version2 completes scoring but fails the stricter mean-length quality gate while exact-match results remain passed.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-failed-gate.png)

The newer ceiling of 3 fails against the same mean of 3.67. Job completion, quality-gate success and canonical exact-match results are separate outcomes; v1 remains unchanged.

5.  In **Assessment job**, select the earlier version 1 job and confirm that it still records version 1 and its original definition.

Use the same historical suite version when you want a [paired comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) under an unchanged policy. A different version may be intentionally useful, but it is a different scoring definition.

## 4\. Inspect monitoring history

Project [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/overview.md) summarizes native trace activity and feedback. Monitoring on this page summarizes saved scoring jobs and gates; the two views answer different questions.

1.  Open **Evals → Overview** and choose **Monitoring**.
2.  Read **Scoring history**, including the run, scoring definition, job status and quality gate.
3.  Select a history entry to expand its scorecard, then choose **Open run**.
4.  In the opened run’s **Assessment job**, select the matching suite version and time. **Open run** initially shows that run’s latest job, which may use a newer policy than the history entry you opened.
5.  Refresh, reselect that historical job if needed, and confirm its suite version and gate result remain available.

![Monitoring retains completed v1 passed and v2 failed jobs, with the older scorecard expanded.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-monitoring.png)

Select a history entry to inspect its retained definition and gate. Open run starts on the latest job, so reselect the historical Assessment job when following an older entry.

Monitoring here is saved-output scoring history. It does not automatically schedule production target calls, continuously test a deployment, or establish model drift. Those claims require separate instrumentation and an explicitly supported execution workflow.

## Failures and recovery

-   A stale suite-version edit requires reloading the latest saved definition before another version is admitted.
-   **Retry saved request** checks an unresolved suite save. Do not create a different suite merely to bypass an uncertain response.
-   One scoring job per organization can be active at a time. Wait for it to finish or use the [cooperative scoring stop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/stopping-and-recovery.md).
-   A policy criterion requires its policy instructions. Missing assessments, provider errors and incomplete coverage need review; they are not Boolean passes.

Next, [compare matching suite jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) or [triage recorded quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

---

# Annotate a native trace

> Add typed human feedback or an expectation to a retained trace and recover an uncertain save without creating a duplicate.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/trace-annotations/)

Current beta console · member/admin/owner writes; authorized roles read

Attach a human opinion or expected behavior to a native trace, including a conversation trace that has no dataset evaluation run. This is separate from [assigned human-review queues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md). Saving an annotation does not execute a target or model.

## Before you start

Any authorized customer role can read annotations. A **member/admin/owner** can add one in a ready, writable project. Archived projects are read-only. Start from an existing trace you are authorized to inspect.

The screenshots annotate the retained **recall → BLUE** trace from the [native conversation walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md#3-group-recorded-conversations). Adding feedback to that trace does not repeat either conversation turn.

## 1\. Open the annotation form

1.  Open **Evals → Traces**, confirm **Project**, and open the intended trace’s **Trace details**.
2.  Choose **Add annotation** in **Annotations**.
3.  Select **Annotation type**: **Feedback** or **Expectation**.
4.  Enter **Name**: start with a lowercase letter, then use lowercase letters, digits or underscores, up to 60 characters. `exact_match` is reserved.

![Actual Add annotation form for response\_correct with Feedback, Pass, rationale and Save annotation.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-trace-annotation-form.png)

This real form rates the saved recall response. Save appends feedback to that trace without calling the target again.

## 2\. Enter the value and save once

| Type | Fields | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Feedback → Pass or fail | Rating: Pass / Fail; optional rationale | A Boolean human judgment |
| Feedback → Number | Numeric rating; optional rationale | A numeric human judgment |
| Feedback → Text | Feedback text; optional rationale | A textual observation |
| Expectation | Expected response or behavior | Text describing what should have happened |

1.  Choose **Value type** for Feedback and enter its **Rating** or **Feedback text**. **Rationale (optional)** supports up to 2,000 characters.
2.  For Expectation, enter **Expected response or behavior**, up to 4,000 characters. It has no separate rationale field.
3.  Review the trace, name, type and value, then select **Save annotation** once. **Close** leaves the form without submitting it.
4.  Read the saved annotation’s type, value and author. Your own annotation shows **You**. Refresh and reopen the same trace to confirm it remains in **Annotations**.

![Refreshed trace details retaining response\_correct, Feedback, You, Pass and the saved rationale.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-trace-annotation-saved.png)

After page refresh and a supported Refresh traces recovery, the same Boolean annotation remains beside the original recall input and BLUE output.

## 3\. Recover an uncertain save

An uncertain response can leave the form locked to its original submission. Use **Retry annotation** for that same submission; it retains the request identity and reads back the corresponding native assessment.

If the form closed successfully but a later trace read fails, use **Refresh traces**, reopen the trace and inspect **Annotations**. A read failure does not establish that the save failed.

If that form/browser intent is no longer available, reopen the trace and inspect its existing annotations before beginning a fresh submission. A new submission creates another annotation rather than editing the previous one. The current UI does not offer annotation edit/delete; do not use repeated fresh saves as a retry strategy.

## Understand what changed

Feedback and Expectation are retained human assessments. They do not rewrite span inputs/outputs, published dataset answers, canonical evaluation results, a scoring job or a review queue. Feedback can contribute to the native dashboard’s typed quality summary; Boolean false feedback can contribute to Quality issues. Expectation text is not projected as a feedback score.

A human annotation is an opinion or expectation, not a model judgment or independently verified security finding. Keep sensitive values within the trace’s authorized audience.

Continue with [Evals dashboard summaries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/overview.md) or [quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

---

# Inspect traces and sessions

> Search native trace evidence, inspect spans, group recorded sessions, save views and export bounded results.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/traces-and-sessions/)

Current beta console · all customer roles read/export; member+ saves views

Use the trace explorer to follow recorded requests and inspect the spans, inputs, outputs and assessments behind an evaluation. Group by a reported session ID when you need a conversation view. These reads do not execute a target again.

## Before you start

Any customer role can inspect authorized native traces in the current beta console. Your organization must have ready Evals setup and retained trace evidence in the selected project. **Members** or higher can save views; viewers can use organization-shared views. You do not need a separate MLflow login or MLflow credentials.

Complete a [first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) to create fresh evidence. Not every request reports a session, user, token count, cost or model identity. Missing fields stay unavailable.

## 1\. Find the trace selection

1.  Open **Evals → Traces** and confirm the project.
2.  Enter distinctive input/output text in **Search trace content**.
3.  Choose **Trace state** or **Trace order** if needed.
4.  Open **More filters** for **Session ID**, **User ID**, **Minimum latency (ms)**, **Time window**, **Boolean assessment** and **Assessment value**.
5.  Click **Apply filters** and read the applied-filter summary and coverage note. Use **Reset** to clear filters deliberately.

![HELLO content and OK state filters select one real retained native trace in the archived teaching project.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-filtered.png)

The applied HELLO and OK filters return one recorded request. Archiving preserves this evidence; reading it does not rerun the target.

Start with a narrow, known request or recent time window. An empty selection is not proof that the agent never ran; confirm the organization, project, filters and trace retention.

## 2\. Inspect native execution evidence

1.  Open a trace from the table to display **Trace details**.
2.  Begin with **Inputs / outputs** and compare the recorded values with the saved evaluation result.
3.  Inspect available **Overview**, **Messages**, **Attributes**, **Events** and **Usage** tabs. Use the span/tree or timeline controls shown by the inspector for the recorded trace structure.
4.  Expand **Trace assessments and metadata** to inspect retained feedback and identifiers.
5.  Choose **Download native payload** when you need the retained native evidence for an authorized review.

The capture below shows **Trace details** opened from the filtered trace table, with two native spans and the recorded input/output. For a trace attached to an evaluation result, you can also use the run’s **Results → Inspect → View trace** path.

![Trace details opened from the filtered table shows two native spans and retained HELLO input with hello output.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-table-inspector.png)

The trace-table inspector retains the real input/output and two spans. There are 0 model spans and reported tokens are unavailable; missing usage is not zero usage.

A missing usage field is not zero usage. Reported model names, costs and span events describe what was retained; they do not independently verify billing, deployed code or a business-side effect. Treat trace downloads as potentially sensitive and share them according to your organization’s policy.

To append a human rating or expected behavior to a trace, follow [Annotate traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/trace-annotations.md).

## 3\. Group recorded conversations

Traces with the same reported session ID can appear together in **Sessions**. In this example, one turn stores `BLUE` and the next recalls it.

1.  Return to Traces. To inspect a known conversation, open **Filters** (**More filters** to assistive tools), enter its **Session ID** and click **Apply filters**. Set **Group traces by** to **Group by session**.
2.  Inspect **Recorded sessions**, turns, errors and first/last recorded times. This bounded example contains one session, **2** turns, **0** errors and no ungrouped traces.

![One real native conversation session with two turns, zero errors and no ungrouped traces.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-native-session-group.png)

Two real HTTP requests share a reported native session ID. Recorded sessions includes both completed traces; tokens stay unavailable. This uses separately provisioned native instrumentation.

3.  Choose **View turns** to inspect one session while retaining its applied filters.

![Session-filtered trace table showing remember BLUE to Stored BLUE, then recall to BLUE.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-native-session-turns.png)

View turns opens the two persisted requests in the same session. The actual HTTP application stored and recalled BLUE; these reads do not run the application again.

4.  Open each trace to compare the real request and response. Refresh and confirm that both turns remain. **Ungroup traces** returns from Sessions to the individual trace table.

![Real recall trace with a completed chat-turn span, memory span and BLUE response.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-native-session-memory.png)

The recall request retained its real memory operation and BLUE output. There are no model spans, and missing token/cost values remain unavailable.

Sessions require a reported session ID. A set of independent dataset requests is not automatically a multi-turn conversation. If you see **No sessions recorded**, inspect individual traces and confirm that the target/instrumentation reports the session identifiers you expect.

An SDK **CI session** identifies a pytest upload; it is a different identifier from a conversation session. SDK 0.1.2 dataset and inline-check uploads do not forward local trace session metadata. The separate SDK teaching example below therefore has **0 sessions and 1 matching trace without a session ID**. A native integration requires separately provisioned writer access; Martian SDK 0.1.2/API keys do not issue those credentials or provide an equivalent customer trace-ingestion route. Ask your operator about a supported session-bearing integration rather than copying a CI upload ID into this filter.

![Sessions reports zero recorded sessions and one matching trace without a session ID.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-no-sessions.png)

This separate SDK 0.1.2 selection contains one independent evaluation request with no conversation session ID. Its empty state differs from the two-turn native example above, which uses separately provisioned instrumentation.

## 4\. Save a useful view

1.  As a member/admin/owner, choose **Display**; its accessible action is **Columns and view settings**.
2.  In **Display and saved views**, select columns, move them into a useful order, and choose **Compact rows** if desired.
3.  Enter **View name** and choose **Visibility**: **Private** or **Organization**.
4.  Click **Save new view**. Select it later using **Saved trace view**.
5.  After refreshing, select the view again in **Saved trace view**, then confirm its saved filters, columns and density. Refreshing opens the default view; it does not automatically reselect your last saved view. **Update view** saves an authorized revision; **Delete view** requires confirmation.

Private views belong to their creator. Organization views are readable by the organization; mutation still requires ownership or administrator authority. Saving a view does not save a reusable native pagination cursor or grant new trace access.

![Display and saved views shows the retained organization view with chosen columns and comfortable row density.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-saved-view.png)

The member-created organization view retains its filters, column order and density. After refresh, reselect it in Saved trace view to restore those settings.

## 5\. Export a complete bounded selection

1.  Apply filters that produce the selection you want.
2.  Choose **Export CSV** or **Export JSON**.
3.  Inspect the downloaded count and identities against the selection and its coverage note.
4.  If the export is too large, narrow the filters and export again.

Trace exports support up to 1,000 matching traces and reject an oversized selection instead of silently returning the first 1,000. Overview, session grouping and quality-issue aggregates also inspect bounded selections; read their incomplete-coverage labels. Trace table pages contain up to 100 rows.

## Failures and recovery

Use **Refresh traces** after a temporary read failure. A stale cursor or changed session can require starting the search again. Quote/backslash content searches can be constrained by the native stored representation; use a distinctive simpler term, IDs or structured filters when needed. Reading/exporting evidence cannot repair missing telemetry and should not trigger a replacement target run.

If a view save reports **Failed to fetch** or another uncertain result, refresh and inspect **Saved trace view** before saving again. A new save can create another view; confirm whether the earlier one exists first.

Next, [review saved responses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md) or [triage quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

---

# MITRE ATLAS

> Use ATLAS tactics and techniques to describe AI attacks while keeping Martian catalogue IDs, framework references and execution evidence separate.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/frameworks/mitre-atlas/)

MITRE ATLAS is a knowledge base of adversary behavior involving AI systems. It includes techniques concerning prompts, tools, context, models, data and the surrounding supply chain. Use the [official ATLAS site](https://atlas.mitre.org/) and [MITRE’s data repository](https://github.com/mitre-atlas/atlas-data) for the authoritative definitions.

ATLAS and [MITRE ATT&CK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/frameworks/mitre-attack.md) are related MITRE knowledge bases with distinct identifiers and scope. “MITRE” is the organization; it is not a third attack framework alongside those two.

## Read the identifiers

| Identifier | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AML.TA…` | ATLAS tactic: the adversary’s purpose at a stage |
| `AML.T…` | ATLAS technique or sub-technique: a kind of behavior |
| `MT-…` | Martian catalogue technique, such as `MT-07 Document injection` |

An `MT-` entry is not an official ATLAS identifier. Similar wording or a related attack mechanism does not establish a one-to-one match.

## Start with a relevant behavior

| ATLAS reference | Read about the corresponding attack surface |
| --- | --- |
| `AML.T0051` LLM Prompt Injection | [Prompt injection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/prompt-injection.md) |
| `AML.T0051.000` Direct; `AML.T0051.001` Indirect | [Direct](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/direct-prompt-injection.md) and [indirect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/indirect-prompt-injection.md) delivery |
| `AML.T0054` LLM Jailbreak | [Jailbreaks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/jailbreaks.md) |
| `AML.T0053` AI Agent Tool Invocation | [Tool and action abuse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/tool-action-abuse.md) |
| `AML.T0070` RAG Poisoning; `AML.T0080` AI Agent Context Poisoning | [Memory and context poisoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/memory-context-poisoning.md) |
| `AML.T0110` AI Agent Tool Poisoning | [MCP and tool poisoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/mcp-tool-poisoning.md) |
| `AML.T0086` Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation | [Data exfiltration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/data-exfiltration.md) |
| `AML.T0010` Supply Chain Compromise | [Supply chain and backdoors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/supply-chain-backdoors.md) |
| `AML.T0029` Denial of AI Service; `AML.T0034` Cost Harvesting | [Resource exhaustion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/denial-of-service.md) |

These names and IDs were checked against [MITRE’s published ATLAS data](https://github.com/mitre-atlas/atlas-data/blob/main/dist/v6/ATLAS-2026.10.yaml). Each attack page links the relevant entries and explains the narrower Martian support boundary.

## Interpret the Martian view

The console’s **MITRE ATLAS** lens groups the stored catalogue for exploration. Its eight native technique buckets are Injection, Execution, Escalation, Persistence, Collection, Exfiltration, Impact and Evasion. This is a product grouping, not a reproduction of the complete official ATLAS tactic matrix.

Treat displayed anchor references as navigation context. For example, the native Execution bucket uses `AML.T0086`, whose official name concerns exfiltration through tools. That anchor is not an exact official mapping for every technique in the bucket. Use the actual behavior and authoritative entry definition when writing a report.

Selecting a framework lens does not install every ATLAS technique, expand target access or establish that a test ran. Follow [Attack Library coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/coverage.md) to choose available scope, and inspect the run’s actual attempts and evidence.

## Report a mapping responsibly

Record the Martian technique ID, the related ATLAS ID and source edition, the tested surface, and why the relationship applies. Keep the framework reference separate from the observed result and any independent outcome check. When only part of an ATLAS entry was exercised, describe that part.

These documentation relationships are editorial guidance. They do not represent MITRE endorsement, exhaustive coverage or a certification. Continue with the [attack reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/attacks.md) or [assessment configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/configure.md).

---

# MITRE ATT&CK

> Relate AI attack evidence to conventional infrastructure behavior without confusing ATT&CK, ATLAS and Martian identifiers.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/frameworks/mitre-attack/)

[MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/) organizes adversary tactics and techniques based on observed behavior across enterprise, mobile and industrial environments. It is useful when an AI attack interacts with accounts, endpoints, cloud services, code execution or other conventional infrastructure.

[MITRE ATLAS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/frameworks/mitre-atlas.md) focuses on AI-related adversary behavior. The knowledge bases can overlap; an AI system is also software running in an environment with identities, data and tools.

## ATT&CK includes prompt injection

The current Enterprise knowledge base includes [T1699 Direct Prompt Injection](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1699/) and [T1698 Indirect Prompt Injection](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1698/). Avoid assuming that prompt attacks appear only in ATLAS.

| Reference system | Direct injection example | Indirect injection example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ATT&CK | `T1699` | `T1698` |
| ATLAS | `AML.T0051.000` | `AML.T0051.001` |
| Martian | Related entries include `MT-01` | Related entries include `MT-07`, `MT-08`, `MT-09` |

The table relates delivery mechanisms. It does not make the identifiers interchangeable or claim that each Martian entry implements the full official technique.

## Follow the behavior across systems

Suppose a synthetic document redirects an agent into sending a protected demo record through a tool. Investigate the chain as separate observations:

1.  The agent consumed the attacker-controlled document.
2.  The document changed the agent’s behavior.
3.  A tool request targeted an unauthorized destination.
4.  The receiving system confirms a transfer, if that evidence is available.

The first two observations concern [indirect injection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/indirect-prompt-injection.md); the latter observations concern [tool abuse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/tool-action-abuse.md) and [exfiltration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/data-exfiltration.md). Choose additional infrastructure references only when the evidence supports the specific technique’s definition. A printed shell command does not prove command execution.

## What Martian’s lens establishes

The current library offers a **MITRE ATLAS** view. This reference page does not add an ATT&CK selector, an ATT&CK test pack or general infrastructure penetration-testing support. An approved agent endpoint also does not authorize probing its surrounding hosts or accounts.

Use the [available catalogue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/coverage.md), [supported targets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/supported-targets.md) and the actual approved scenario to define scope. Treat an ATT&CK mapping as an annotation on observed behavior, with the framework ID and source kept separate from Martian’s technique ID and execution status.

Continue with [ATLAS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/frameworks/mitre-atlas.md), the [attack reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/attacks.md) and [evidence interpretation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md).

---

# NIST AI RMF

> Place Martian testing evidence within Govern, Map, Measure and Manage without treating a library lens as a complete risk program.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/frameworks/nist-ai-rmf/)

The [NIST AI Risk Management Framework Core](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/) organizes risk work into **Govern, Map, Measure and Manage**. These functions apply across the lifecycle and inform one another. They are not four test suites or a mandatory sequence of steps.

The [NIST Playbook](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/) offers suggested actions. Use the official sources for their full scope; a red-team assessment supplies only part of the evidence a risk program needs.

## Use a concrete workflow

Consider a support agent connected to a synthetic order system. A useful application of the functions is:

| Function | Example decision or evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Govern | Assign the owner of the approval policy, testing authorization, risk acceptance and change review |
| Map | Identify users, data, tools, trust boundaries and the consequences of an unauthorized credit |
| Measure | Run a bounded compatible test and inspect actual attempts, scorer limits and independent state checks |
| Manage | Prioritize the observed failure, repair the relevant boundary, retain a regression case and review residual uncertainty |

These are applied examples for this workflow, not replacements for NIST’s categories and subcategories. Governance remains relevant throughout the other functions.

## Interpret the Martian lens

The current Attack Library has a **NIST** view using stored Map, Measure and Manage tags. It does not include a Govern bucket in that native technique lens. That is a limitation of the product grouping, not a change to the four-function framework.

Selecting the lens does not assess every AI RMF outcome or determine organizational maturity. A technique tagged Manage is not evidence that remediation, ownership or risk acceptance has already happened.

## Retain useful evidence

Connect the tested rule to the actual agent and environment, approved scope, relevant data boundaries and accountable owner. Keep the run and dataset revisions, attempts, scores, failed observations and outcome checks together where the workflow supports them.

After a failure, record the remediation and the conditions under which it was checked again. A successful retest of one case does not erase untested interfaces or unknown side effects. Preserve incomplete results so a later decision can account for them.

For ongoing evaluation, use [versioned datasets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md), [regression cases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/regression-cases.md) and [comparisons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) where appropriate. Scoring quality and operational risk ownership remain separate responsibilities.

The framework relationship is guidance for organizing evidence, not a NIST endorsement or certification. Continue with [attack selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/attacks.md) and [reproduction and limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/reproduction-and-limits.md).

---

# OWASP Agentic Top 10

> Understand official Agentic risk names, native Martian tags and the boundaries involved in tools, identity, memory and coordination.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/frameworks/owasp-agentic/)

The [OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026](https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/) focuses on risks in systems that plan, act and coordinate. It complements the [LLM Top 10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/frameworks/owasp-llm.md) rather than replacing it.

## The official entries

| OWASP entry | Related reading in this reference |
| --- | --- |
| ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack | [Prompt injection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/prompt-injection.md) |
| ASI02 Tool Misuse and Exploitation | [Tool and action abuse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/tool-action-abuse.md) |
| ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse | [Privilege escalation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/privilege-escalation.md) |
| ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities | [Supply chain and backdoors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/supply-chain-backdoors.md) |
| ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution (RCE) | [Tool abuse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/tool-action-abuse.md), with independent execution evidence |
| ASI06 Memory and Context Poisoning | [Memory and context poisoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/memory-context-poisoning.md) |
| ASI07 Insecure Inter-Agent Communication | [Multi-agent handoff boundaries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/multi-agent-attacks.md) |
| ASI08 Cascading Failures | [Propagation across agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/multi-agent-attacks.md) |
| ASI09 Human-Agent Trust Exploitation | [Human manipulation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/human-manipulation.md) |
| ASI10 Rogue Agents | [Multi-agent behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/multi-agent-attacks.md) and [objective-related limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/reasoning-alignment-subversion.md) |

The names identify the official entries in the [OWASP publication](https://genai.owasp.org/download/52117/?tmstv=1765059207). The reading links are editorial relationships. They do not declare complete coverage or equate every attack on that page with the corresponding risk.

## Native tags use some different wording

Martian’s stored list currently includes `ASI02`, `ASI03`, `ASI04`, `ASI06`, `ASI07` and `ASI08`. Some console display labels are shorter or use different terminology from the official publication:

| Native label | Official entry to consult |
| --- | --- |
| ASI03 Privilege compromise | ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse |
| ASI07 Trust boundary | ASI07 Insecure Inter-Agent Communication |
| ASI08 Agent collusion | ASI08 Cascading Failures |

In particular, **Agent collusion is not the official name of ASI08**. Do not copy that display label into a report as an official definition. Inspect the actual scenario and evidence to decide which risk applies.

An absent `ASI01` or `ASI09` tag does not prove that an adjacent injection or approval technique is irrelevant. Conversely, a related technique does not establish comprehensive coverage of an official entry. `MT-36 Worker collusion` remains a declared gap.

## Define the boundary before selecting scope

For a tool test, identify the operation and authority. For an agent handoff, identify the sender, receiver, message provenance and scope. For a memory test, identify the store and later read. For a human approval, compare the displayed request with the exact action.

Use an approved synthetic scenario that actually exposes the required surface. Keep a proposed action, a dispatched call and an independently verified effect separate in the result. A passing judge or framework filter is not proof of enforcement at every boundary.

Continue with [Attack Library coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/coverage.md), [the attack families](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/attacks.md) and [assessment evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md).

---

# OWASP LLM Top 10

> Use the OWASP LLM application risks to organize testing, with explicit limits on Martian tags and executable coverage.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/frameworks/owasp-llm/)

The [OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications](https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/) describes application risk categories. A category is broader than a single attack payload or executable test. Use it to ask what could fail, then choose a supported technique and define observable evidence.

## The 2025 risk categories

The names below identify the official OWASP entries. The Martian reading links are editorial starting points, not a complete crosswalk or a claim that every category is covered.

| OWASP entry | Start investigating |
| --- | --- |
| LLM01 Prompt Injection | [Untrusted instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/prompt-injection.md) |
| LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure | [Protected data and destinations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/data-exfiltration.md) |
| LLM03 Supply Chain | [Dependencies, tools and artifacts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/supply-chain-backdoors.md) |
| LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning | [Poisoned context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/memory-context-poisoning.md) and [training-related limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/reasoning-alignment-subversion.md) |
| LLM05 Improper Output Handling | [Unsafe tool arguments and actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/tool-action-abuse.md); also review the consuming application’s output handling |
| LLM06 Excessive Agency | [Tool scope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/tool-action-abuse.md) and [delegated authority](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/privilege-escalation.md) |
| LLM07 System Prompt Leakage | Review what prompt content is exposed and whether it contains protected information |
| LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses | [Retrieval poisoning and access boundaries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/memory-context-poisoning.md) |
| LLM09 Misinformation | Compare answers with authoritative data; inspect [scorer limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/guardrail-judge-evasion.md) |
| LLM10 Unbounded Consumption | [Time, cost and resource exhaustion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/attacks/denial-of-service.md) |

Use [OWASP’s official risk pages](https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/) for definitions and mitigations. For example, [LLM06](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/) concerns agency granted to an application; it is not simply another name for a jailbreak.

## Read Martian’s tags accurately

The current selectable list uses `LLM01`, `LLM02` and `LLM08` on related entries. It also contains Agentic `ASI…` tags and the native `business` and `social` groupings. Those last two are Martian labels, not official OWASP IDs.

The **OWASP LLM + Agentic** library view filters and groups stored entries. It does not establish complete Top 10 coverage. In particular, documentation about supply chains, model poisoning, misinformation or resource exhaustion must not be read as proof that a corresponding dedicated test is selectable.

## Turn a category into a test

Write a concrete rule and outcome, such as “a viewer must not receive another synthetic tenant’s record.” Identify the actual retrieval or tool boundary, select a compatible available technique, and compare the result with that rule. Record any unsupported surface or missing observation explicitly.

Keep prompt disclosure distinct from data compromise: exposed instructions may reveal useful implementation details, but a claim of secret disclosure needs an actual protected value and an unauthorized reader. Likewise, an incorrect answer and a downstream execution flaw require different checks.

After a supported run, retain the underlying evidence with its OWASP reference. A framework label or a passing set of selected cases is not a security certification.

Continue with the [OWASP Agentic Top 10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/frameworks/owasp-agentic.md), [Attack Library coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/coverage.md) and [results and scores](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md).

---

# Accept an invitation and sign in

> Join the correct organization, sign in, and check your available role.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/get-started/access/)

Current beta console · All invited customer roles

Finish with a signed-in Martian workspace and a role that matches your task. This guide is for invited users of the current beta. Accounts require an invitation; there is no public self-service sign-up.

## Before you begin

-   Ask your organization admin for an invitation to the correct workspace. A new organization owner receives an organization invitation from the platform administrator.
-   Need your first workspace? Use the **REQUEST\_A\_DROP()** contact option on [martiansecurity.ai](https://martiansecurity.ai/) or email [founders@martiansecurity.ai](mailto:founders@martiansecurity.ai) with your company, agent purpose and staging availability. Do not include credentials or customer records.
-   Use a desktop browser for the application. These docs also work on a narrow screen.
-   Open the exact invitation link privately. It contains account-enrollment authority; do not post it in a screenshot, issue or shared document.

## Join your workspace

1.  Open your invitation link and confirm the intended organization and recipient. An expired, revoked or incomplete link cannot create an account; ask the inviter for a replacement.
2.  Fill in **Your name**, **Password**, and **Confirm password**. Use at least 12 characters. For a new organization invitation, also enter **Organization name**, **Organization subdomain**, and **About your organization**.
3.  Submit the account form. Wait for the completion page. For an existing organization it confirms **You joined your organization**. A new account can be ready before Evals setup has finished; read the status instead of submitting the invitation again.
4.  Use the sign-in address shown on that page. Keep your organization address for future visits.

![Organization invitation form with synthetic owner and organization details; password fields are empty.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-organization-setup.png)

Enter your organization and account details to accept an owner invitation.

![Workspace ready confirmation after the invited owner created Martian Docs Lab.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-workspace-ready.png)

Use the sign-in address shown after creating your organization.

## Sign in and check access

1.  At the sign-in screen enter **Email** and **Password**, then select **Sign in**.

![Martian Security sign-in screen with empty Email and Password fields](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-sign-in.png)

Sign in with your invited workspace account.

2.  Check the organization shown in the account area at the bottom of the sidebar. An account in another organization does not gain access to this workspace’s records.
3.  Open **Overview**. The navigation available to you follows your role. [Permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md) explains which tasks need a member, admin or owner.
4.  If your next task is Evals, open **Evals** and wait for the workspace’s setup status. **Refresh setup** reads readiness; it does not grant missing access or complete a failed setup automatically.

![Signed-in Martian Docs Lab showing Default project, owner role and the Evals Runs page.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-workspace.png)

Open Evals and select a project, such as the Default project.
