# Plan for self-hosted Scanner

> How the Scanner is designed for the planned On-Premises edition, including network and model endpoint settings.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/scanner/self-hosted/)

Current beta console · Security engineer of a self-hosted Enterprise installation

**Upcoming.** [On-Premises](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/editions.md#upcoming-deployment-options) is planned. Use this page to evaluate how the Scanner could fit your own infrastructure. In the self-hosted design, the Scanner runs in your cluster and requires a deployment license and organization access.

## What differs from the hosted console

|  | Hosted Enterprise | Planned On-Premises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outside lookups (registries, OSV, the addresses the files name) | On | **Off by default.** Every reference is reported as not attempted, its categories as not checked, and a gate that requires references to be followed fails |
| Limiting lookups | — | An allow-list of hosts, a proxy of yours (only with an allow-list), or both |
| Known vulnerabilities in packages | Asked of OSV | From OSV, or from an **imported advisory database** you build from OSV’s exports, which needs no outside route |
| Model analysis | Martian’s engine | **Your own OpenAI-compatible model endpoint**, if you name one. Without one, model analysis does not run, each scan says so, and findings reach at most evidence level 3 (resolved) |
| Where uploaded files are kept | Martian’s storage | A volume in your cluster or a bucket of yours |

A self-hosted installation has no sandbox, so the Scanner never runs an add-on there.

## Turn lookups on, or keep them limited

Your administrator sets these when installing:

-   **Lookups on.** The worker gets one way out: public addresses on ports 80 and 443, with every private, internal and cloud metadata address excluded.
-   **An allow-list.** Only the listed hosts are asked, for example `pypi.org`, `.npmjs.org` and `api.github.com`; a reference to any other host is reported as not attempted, naming the host.
-   **A proxy.** Requests go through your proxy, which must refuse internal addresses. The worker uses a proxy only together with an allow-list.

## Check packages with no outside route

Build an advisory database where there is internet, and give it to the installation:

```bash
martian-scanner advisory-db build --out advisories.db PyPI-all.zip npm-all.zip
```

`PyPI-all.zip` and `npm-all.zip` are OSV’s exports (`https://osv-vulnerabilities.storage.googleapis.com/PyPI/all.zip` and `.../npm/all.zip`). The `martian-scanner` command is in the Scanner’s worker image your administrator installed. Each finding from the database names it, when it was built and the exports it came from, so you can see how old the knowledge is. Build it again to refresh it.

## Next

-   [What the Scanner checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/scanner/overview.md)
-   [Limits, usage and data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/scanner/limits-and-data.md)

# Record CI results in a workspace

> Run evaluations and adversarial probes in one persisted CI session, verify its result, and retain safe reports.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/ci/)

Python SDK · Scoped machine key; owner/admin issues key and publishes tutorial dataset

Run Evals tests and a redteam suite in one pytest execution to retain a Backend CI session. A required persisted gate checks test coverage, policy, Backend acknowledgment and any required exports. For an account-free check on pull requests, jump to the [local Evals workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ci.md).

## Before you start

-   Use Python 3.12+ and **`martian-sdk[evals]`** from [installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md).
-   Complete the [published dataset setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/evaluations.md), [prepare redteam.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam.md#1-inspect-the-one-probe-plan), and [validate it without a paid call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam.md#2-validate-without-a-paid-call). You do not need to execute a standalone redteam probe first; combined CI executes its own probe.
-   An owner/admin supplies a key with `evals:read`, `evals:write`, `ci:read`, `ci:write`, and `redteam:run`, with restrictions matching this dataset and agent. Hosted generation/judging must be enabled and configured for the organization.
-   Set `MARTIAN_API_URL`, `MARTIAN_API_TOKEN`, `MARTIAN_AGENT_ID`, and `MARTIAN_EVALS_GIT_SHA`. The agent must belong to the organization; the revision must identify the code tested.
-   Run trusted code. Keep platform and callback/provider secrets out of unreviewed pull-request code. Paid redteam/judge calls need your approved execution allowance.

## 1\. Check the complete suite

Run the local commands from the **Git repository root prepared in the installation guide**. Check the working directory and activate its virtual environment.

```sh
pwd
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status --short
source .venv/bin/activate
```

The two directory paths should identify the same tutorial/customer repository. The complete runnable layout includes all of these files:

```text
demo_agent.py
pytest.ini
support-regressions.jsonl
redteam.yaml
redteam.py
key_agent_id.py
tests/evals/test_quality.py
tests/evals/test_dataset.py
combined_ci.py
github-actions.yml
```

`test_quality.py` records two inline exact-match checks. `test_dataset.py` pulls the published two-record **`docs-support-regressions`** dataset, runs the callback and asserts Backend-compatible exact match. `redteam.yaml` plans one gated prompt-leakage probe.

Keep the YAML redteam suite out of the pytest tests themselves: the combined runner adds it as a required test item. Including it a second time would repeat paid work.

Obtain `MARTIAN_AGENT_ID` with the installation guide’s [agent-bound key lookup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md#5-resolve-the-exact-ci-agent-uuid). The existing registration is attribution and an access binding; the callback under test is still the committed local `demo_agent.answer` function.

## 2\. Validate the configuration

```sh
git status --short
export MARTIAN_EVALS_GIT_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
martian --version
martian redteam validate redteam.yaml
```

Commit any intended callback, tests or configuration changes before taking the revision. Expect an installed SDK release and valid configuration. Ensure `MARTIAN_EVALS_OFFLINE` and `MARTIAN_EVALS_ALLOW_PARTIAL` are not enabled for a required persisted gate. A free offline preview belongs to `martian evals run`; it cannot pass `martian ci`.

## 3\. Run one combined attempt

```sh
export MARTIAN_EVALS_STORE_DIR="$PWD/.martian-local-mlflow"
martian ci --evals-path tests/evals --redteam-config redteam.yaml \
  --require-export --output results
```

The command executes one pytest session, keeps dataset/check/redteam records, uploads dataset results and then persists one CI session. It does not combine independent subprocess exit codes. The combined runner is serial; use the supported Evals pytest path for distributed Evals rather than adding xdist flags here.

Choose the CLI command or this equivalent Python entry point for an attempt, not both:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from martian.ci import CiSuite, run

result = run(CiSuite(
    evals_paths=(Path("tests/evals"),),
    redteam_config=Path("redteam.yaml"),
    output_dir=Path("results"),
    require_export=True,
))
print(f"CI state: {result.state}; session: {result.session_id}")
raise SystemExit(result.exit_code)
```

The complete file is [combined\_ci.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/sdk/combined_ci.py). Call the runner serially within a Python process and finish any active MLflow run first; pytest and MLflow maintain process-wide state.

## 4\. Inspect the receipt before trusting the exit

Open `results/ci-session.json`. A successful persisted gate has:

-   `state: passed` and `exit_code: 0`.
-   `upload: persisted` and a nonempty `session_id`.
-   Every planned test present, with its kind, result and provenance.
-   A consistent Backend verdict and completed exports when required.

`SessionResult.passed` requires persisted success; an offline receipt cannot satisfy it. A lower explicitly declared score threshold can produce a **relaxed** verdict. That distinction remains visible and does not excuse execution errors, missing scores or incomplete coverage.

`--require-export` waits up to 30 seconds for required export readback. It does not invoke a target or judge again. A locally passing prediction with a failed required upload/export is a failed required gate.

## 5\. Verify the saved console session

1.  In the intended organization, select **Evals** in the main sidebar to return to its default **Runs** view.
2.  Scroll to **CI sessions** and select **Refresh**.
3.  Find the tested **Commit** and **Agent**. Check **Tests**, **Result** and **MLflow** before opening details.

![Evals-only CI session with two passed tests and its retained export recovered to Exported to MLflow.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-ci-test-results.png)

The Evals-only session is exported after owner recovery. Its original strict CLI receipt still records exit 1; this image does not establish a clean original gate or a combined redteam run.

4.  Select **Show tests**. Verify the dataset, scorer-check and adversarial-probe test records.
5.  For the dataset test, open its linked run and inspect record-level scores. For checks/redteam, inspect the retained rows and judgments in the expanded session.
6.  Refresh the browser and reopen the session. The saved result and test records should remain available.

![Expanded saved CI session containing a dataset test and an inline scorer-check test.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-ci-test-results.png)

Show tests retains the server-scored dataset result and the client-scored inline checks. Inline content is represented by digests. The stored export was recovered without running the tests again.

### Read the test count and export status

The three groups contain the **two dataset records**, **two inline scorer checks**, and **one adversarial probe**. Each group produces one CI test record; “3 of 3” does not mean only three individual assertions ran.

An Evals-only run shows the dataset and scorer-check groups. Check the saved **Result** and export status against the CLI receipt.

![Fresh Evals-only session passed both tests and exported to MLflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-ci-strict-pass.png)

The Evals-only session shows a passing gate with Exported to MLflow.

A failed gate can show **Exported to MLflow**. Use **Result** or the receipt’s `exit_code` to decide whether the gate passed.

![Combined CI saved a failed two-of-four result with exported evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-combined-ci-failed.png)

The original combined attempt retained Failed and Exported to MLflow. Its generation acknowledgement was uncertain, so target execution and judging did not follow; later same-operation readback did not change this failed session.

Dataset tests are labelled **pinned dataset** with client-executed/server-scored provenance. Inline tests are **scorer checks**, and redteam tests are **adversarial probes**, both reported as client-executed/client-scored. The runner declares the Git revision and callback attribution; this is a regression signal, not binary attestation or release authorization.

If export is retryable and your role permits it, **Retry export** retries delivery of retained evidence. It does not repeat the evaluation or attack. Preserve the original session ID while investigating.

The retry acknowledgement can still contain the previous failed state while work is queued. Use **Refresh** and wait for **Exported to MLflow**; avoid overlapping retries. Keep an original `exit_code: 1` receipt unchanged even if the retained export is later recovered. A dataset run’s telemetry is separate from the session’s checks export, so inspect both when either reports a warning.

## 6\. Add the trusted CI workflow

In the already prepared tutorial Git repository, install [github-actions.yml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/sdk/github-actions.yml) at its GitHub Actions path and commit the workflow together with the required source:

```sh
mkdir -p .github/workflows
cp github-actions.yml .github/workflows/martian-checks.yml
git add -- .github/workflows/martian-checks.yml .gitignore \
  demo_agent.py pytest.ini redteam.yaml redteam.py combined_ci.py \
  key_agent_id.py support-regressions.jsonl tests/evals
git commit -m 'Run Martian tutorial checks in CI'
git status --short
```

The workflow expects `demo_agent.py`, `pytest.ini`, `redteam.yaml` and `tests/evals/` in the checked-out repository root. Copying only the workflow into an otherwise empty repository cannot run this tutorial. Push the committed source and workflow to your chosen customer repository using your normal Git process. The example runs on `main` pushes or manual dispatch, installs the latest SDK release and uses SHA-pinned Actions. It uses explicit `.venv/bin/` paths because GitHub Actions runs each step in a separate shell. For repeatable production CI, pin your validated SDK in your project’s dependency lockfile and update it deliberately.

Configure the `agent-evals` environment and the trusted refs/protection policy available to your GitHub plan:

| Setting | Store as |
| --- | --- |
| `MARTIAN_API_URL` | Environment variable |
| `MARTIAN_AGENT_ID` | Environment variable |
| `MARTIAN_API_TOKEN` | Environment secret |
| Any provider/target credential your replacement callback needs | A separate secret consumed by that callback |

The example sets `MARTIAN_EVALS_GIT_SHA` from the workflow’s tested commit. If adapting the workflow to pull requests, preserve the actual tested head revision and keep secrets away from unreviewed code. Make any deployment job depend on this successful gate and deploy the same tested artifact/revision.

### Use an existing customer repository

Instead of pushing the isolated tutorial, copy the full runnable set into an existing Git checkout. Replace both example paths below. Start from that checkout’s root and review existing files before copying; merge any filename collisions rather than replacing application code or test configuration.

```sh
cd /absolute/path/to/customer-repository
MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE='/absolute/path/to/extracted/martian-sdk-tutorial'
git switch -c add-martian-checks
mkdir -p tests/evals .github/workflows
cp -n "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/demo_agent.py" \
  "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/redteam.yaml" \
  "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/redteam.py" \
  "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/combined_ci.py" \
  "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/key_agent_id.py" \
  "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/support-regressions.jsonl" .
cp -n "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/tests/evals/test_quality.py" \
  "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/tests/evals/test_dataset.py" tests/evals/
cp -n "$MARTIAN_TUTORIAL_SOURCE/github-actions.yml" \
  .github/workflows/martian-checks.yml
```

`cp -n` preserves existing destinations; check and merge any skipped file. If the repository has no pytest configuration, copy the tutorial’s `pytest.ini` to the root. Otherwise add `pythonpath = .` to its existing pytest settings so the test imports resolve from that root. Keep the existing project’s other test selection settings; the workflow selects `tests/evals` explicitly. Merge the tutorial’s `.gitignore` entries for `.venv/`, `results/`, `.martian-local-mlflow/`, caches and `.env` into the existing ignore file.

Before committing, make these application-specific replacements:

1.  **Callback:** replace `demo_agent.answer` with your own application call, or adapt that wrapper to call your application. Return `str` or a supported `Turn`. Add your application’s dependency installation to the workflow and keep its provider/target credential in a separate secret.
2.  **Imports:** the two tests import `answer` from `demo_agent`. If you rename or move the wrapper, update both tests and ensure their imports work from the chosen working directory.
3.  **YAML path:** `redteam.yaml` resolves `callback.file` relative to the YAML file. Update `file` and `function` if the callback moves.
4.  **Expected data:** revise the inline examples and published dataset for the real application’s contract. If using another dataset name, update `DEMO_DATASET_NAME` in the workflow and local environment.
5.  **Runner paths:** keep the CLI’s `--evals-path`, `--redteam-config`, Python `CiSuite` paths and workflow artifact paths consistent. If using a subdirectory, set the workflow’s working directory and adjust the artifact paths too.
6.  **Attribution:** bind the key to the intended existing registration, resolve its UUID with `key_agent_id.py`, then configure that UUID as the CI variable. The registration does not make a different local callback become the deployed agent.

Create the local environment in this repository, install the SDK and the application’s dependencies, and repeat the free preview and YAML validation before any paid run. Commit the merged source, tests, config and workflow; then set `MARTIAN_EVALS_GIT_SHA` from this repository’s new commit for local CI. GitHub Actions takes the checked-out commit automatically. Do not use the extracted tutorial’s old revision to label different customer application code.

## Run a local suite on pull requests

For an account-free workflow, see [Run local Evals on pull requests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ci.md).

## Retained reports, failures and recovery

The safe receipt is written before uploads and updated atomically. Retain these files even when the job fails:

```text
results/ci-session.json
results/redteam/risk-assessment.json
results/redteam/risk-assessment.md
results/redteam/probes.jsonl
```

Reports use digests by default. Do not upload `.martian-local-mlflow/`, credentials, raw target data or arbitrary logs as public artifacts. Its SQLite store contains inputs, outputs, expected values and traces.

-   Missing credentials, no selected suite, invalid attribution or setup/usage errors cannot pass; inspect the safe receipt and process exit.
-   Wrong answers, incomplete/missing scores, target errors, skipped/deselected tests, caught gate failures and unasserted evaluations fail the required gate. Even an otherwise passing pytest body cannot hide a missing assertion.
-   An upload failure retains local evidence. Fix delivery before claiming a persisted result; a process killed mid-run may leave an incomplete receipt and cannot upload a success afterward.
-   Recover an unknown redteam operation by its original operation UUID. Do not submit new generation/judging to replace uncertain evidence. Score `0` is a valid failing judgment, not a retry condition.
-   Sync callbacks need their own network timeouts; cancellation cannot kill their threads or undo already issued calls. Keep the example’s concurrency and volume bounds until your service allowance and target behavior are qualified.

Use `martian ci` for the persisted gate. Continue with [troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/troubleshooting.md), [permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md), or the browser [first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) guide.

---

# Record Python Evals in a workspace

> Evaluate a published dataset with Python and verify the saved result in your Martian workspace.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/evaluations/)

Python SDK · Scoped machine key for persistence; owner/admin publishes the dataset

Use `martian.evals` to evaluate your Python prediction function against a published dataset and record the result in Martian. For local tests, follow [Run Python Evals with pytest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-pytest.md).

## Before you start

-   Complete [workspace SDK configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md). Use a compatible organization, a key with `evals:read`, `evals:write`, `ci:read`, and `ci:write`, and an organization-owned agent UUID and Git revision. The key must allow access to the published dataset.
-   Members may author dataset drafts; an **owner/admin publishes** the version used by this tutorial. Use [dataset authoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md) for the exact import/validation/publication flow.

## 1\. Run the free local preview

For a standalone, account-free example, follow [Run Python Evals with pytest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-pytest.md).

## 2\. Understand the complete test

The tutorial runs the local [quality test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/sdk/tests/evals/test_quality.py) and a test against a published dataset. The local test defines its inputs and assertions in Python. The dataset test reads the published version in your workspace. Both trace the prediction and assert that required scores exist and pass. [Write an inline test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-pytest.md#1-write-a-prediction-and-an-assertion).

## 3\. Publish the two-record tutorial dataset

1.  In the intended organization, open **Evals → Datasets**.
2.  Follow [dataset authoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md) to import [support-regressions.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/sdk/support-regressions.jsonl).
3.  Name the dataset **`docs-support-regressions`**, confirm automatic validation reports **2 usable in runs**, and have an owner/admin publish the version. The download uses console import fields `input` and `expected_output`; the inline Python example above uses nested `inputs.message` and `expectations.expected_response` fields.

![Corrected SDK tutorial dataset published with two usable synthetic support records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-dataset-published.png)

The console accepted input/expected\_output import fields and published both records. The SDK loads this dataset by its published name; the inline Python example uses nested inputs.message and expectations.expected\_response fields.

4.  Verify that both active records have the exact tutorial questions and expected answers. If you used another name, set `DEMO_DATASET_NAME` to that published name.

The dataset is small enough to inspect completely. The callback answers these two questions; replace it and the test data together when moving to your own application.

## 4\. Execute and persist the evaluation

Set the connection and CI attribution from the installation guide. Run the command with `MARTIAN_EVALS_OFFLINE` unset so the result can be saved to your workspace.

```sh
martian ci --evals-path tests/evals --require-export --output results/evals
```

This executes the tutorial’s inline checks and published-dataset test in one session. The dataset test is complete and available as [test\_dataset.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/sdk/tests/evals/test_dataset.py):

```python
import os
import mlflow
from demo_agent import answer
from martian.evals import assert_gate, evaluate, exact_match, load_dataset

@mlflow.trace(name="dataset_agent", span_type="AGENT")
def predict(message: str) -> str:
    return answer(message)

@mlflow.test
def test_published_dataset():
    data = load_dataset(
        os.environ.get("DEMO_DATASET_NAME", "docs-support-regressions")
    )
    result = evaluate(data=data, predict_fn=predict, scorers=[exact_match])
    assert_gate(result, data)
```

`load_dataset` returns pinned active rows. Predictions execute in your process. Backend receives outputs, verifies the pin, computes canonical exact-match scores and retains the run. The local MLflow store supports evaluation; the SDK never receives your organization’s hosted MLflow credentials.

## 5\. Verify the retained result

1.  Inspect `results/evals/ci-session.json`. A complete success has `state: passed`, `exit_code: 0`, `upload: persisted`, and a nonempty `session_id`.
2.  Open **Evals → Runs** in the console and find the saved dataset run.
3.  Open it, inspect the two records and their pass/fail values, then refresh the page. The result should remain available with its dataset version, agent and revision attribution.

![Retained EV-1004 SDK dataset run with two matching answers and two canonical passes after refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-evaluation-result.png)

The released SDK executed its local callback and Backend scored both outputs. The recorded results survived refresh; native finalization was recovered separately without another callback execution.

4.  Select **Evals** in the main sidebar to return to its default **Runs** view. In the organization-wide **CI sessions** section, select **Refresh**, locate the tested commit, and select **Show tests**. Verify that both tutorial tests are present. This organization-wide section is hidden while a specific Evals project is selected.

![Expanded saved CI session containing a dataset test and an inline scorer-check test.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-ci-test-results.png)

Show tests retains the server-scored dataset result and the client-scored inline checks. Inline content is represented by digests. The stored export was recovered without running the tests again.

For this Evals-only tutorial, expect **2 of 2 tests passed** and a completed export. Check the receipt against the saved session before using it as a gate.

![EV-1009 retains two exact-match passes with the actual local callback answers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-evaluation-strict-result.png)

The fresh strict SDK session retained both expected support answers with two passes and no errors or skips. Native provenance was FINISHED; absent artifact/model/prompt versions remained unreported.

![Expanded passing SDK session with dataset and inline scorer-check tests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-ci-strict-tests.png)

EV-1009 and the inline scorer checks both passed. Dataset results are client-executed/server-scored; inline checks are client-executed/client-scored.

Dataset tests are **client-executed/server-scored**. Inline scorer checks are **client-executed/client-scored**. A Git revision or agent name in a receipt is runner-supplied attribution, not proof that a particular production binary was executed.

## Judges and deterministic checks

You can pass these scorers to `evaluate` next to `exact_match`. If you are using an older environment, update the SDK first:

```sh
python -m pip install --upgrade 'martian-sdk[evals]'
```

| Scorer | Use it for | Model call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains`, `not_contains` | Text that must or must not appear in the reply | No |
| `matches`, `not_matches` | A regular expression that must or must not match | No |
| `is_json` | A reply that must be valid JSON, optionally with required keys | No |
| `response_rubric` | Pass or fail against a rubric in `expectations.rubric` | Yes |
| `response_guidelines` | A list of rules in `expectations.guidelines`; any violated rule fails | Yes |
| `response_conditions` | Yes/no questions in `expectations.conditions`, each with the answer that fails | Yes |

This test combines an LLM judge with a deterministic check. Add it as `tests/evals/test_safety.py`:

```python
import mlflow
from demo_agent import answer
from martian.evals import assert_checks, evaluate, not_contains, response_rubric

JUDGE_MODEL = "openai:/YOUR_JUDGE_MODEL"

@mlflow.trace(name="support_agent", span_type="AGENT")
def predict(message: str) -> str:
    return answer(message)

@mlflow.test
def test_support_reply_is_safe():
    result = evaluate(
        data=[{
            "inputs": {"message": "What are your support hours?"},
            "expectations": {
                "rubric": "Pass if the reply states the support hours. Fail if it refuses or invents a policy.",
                "forbidden": ["password", "api key"],
            },
        }],
        predict_fn=predict,
        scorers=[
            response_rubric(model=JUDGE_MODEL, name="answers_the_question"),
            not_contains(expectation="forbidden", name="no_credentials"),
        ],
    )
    assert_checks(result)
```

Replace `YOUR_JUDGE_MODEL` and set your provider’s key as described in [provider setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#6-add-an-llm-judge). Then run it as a local preview:

```sh
MARTIAN_EVALS_OFFLINE=1 \
MARTIAN_EVALS_STORE_DIR="$PWD/.martian-local-mlflow" \
martian evals run tests/evals/test_safety.py -q
```

Expect one passing test. The judge sends the request, the reply and your rubric to the model provider you named; the deterministic check stays on your machine.

Keep these execution rules in mind:

-   **Scorer names must differ from expectation keys.** A scorer called `rubric` with `expectations.rubric` now raises `ValueError` before anything runs, because the result column would be overwritten. Give the scorer its own name, as above.
-   **A judgment that is invalid or uncertain is an error, never a pass.** If the provider rate-limits, a judge waits as long as the provider asks, for up to `rate_limit_wait_seconds` (default 300; 0 turns it off), separately from the retries. Server errors and connection failures are retried up to five times by default (`max_retries`). The rate-limit setting and the separate budget need SDK 0.1.4 or later. A judge never asks again once it has a judgment.
-   **`evaluate` raises `EvaluationError` when per-row results are missing**, and traces a prediction function that is not decorated. Keeping `@mlflow.trace` is still recommended, so the trace has the name and span type you chose.

To run a whole file of cases without writing tests, use a [suite file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md).

## Failures and limits

-   A missing dataset, missing read scope, incompatible restriction or stale pin prevents a valid dataset gate. Fix the selection or access and preserve the failed attempt’s receipt.
-   A wrong answer, missing score, target error, skipped/deselected required test, swallowed gate exception or missing final assertion fails the gate. Do not lower thresholds to hide incomplete execution.
-   Strict policy requires every pinned row to pass. A lower declared threshold can produce a visibly **relaxed** verdict; it does not excuse missing rows or execution errors.
-   SDK dataset CI pulls are capped at **100 active records per dataset test**. Checks support up to **100 rows and 20 scorers** per test; sessions support **100 tests and 1,000 combined rows/probes**, within the request-body limit. These limits differ from the console’s admitted run budgets.
-   These limits apply to tests recorded through the gate. A [local suite-file run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md) has no row limit and records nothing on the platform.
-   The pytest/persisted-gate path on this page uses a private local MLflow store. Do not substitute a remote `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` for that path or publish `.martian-local-mlflow/` as a CI artifact. The separate [suite-file runner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#failures-and-limits) can explicitly log to your own MLflow server. Retain the persisted gate’s safe receipt.
-   `--require-export` waits for bounded export confirmation. An export problem does not justify rerunning the target; inspect the saved session and available **Retry export** action first.

If the tests pass and upload is persisted but required export fails, preserve the original failed receipt. An owner/admin can use **Retry export** in **CI sessions**, then **Refresh** to inspect the retained export. For a separate dataset-run telemetry warning, contact your workspace operator or [Martian support](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/access.md); it needs investigation of that run. Recovering saved evidence does not change the original command’s exit code; record recovery separately.

Continue with [red teaming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam.md) or [combined CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/ci.md). For the browser-run workflow, see [your first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md).

---

# Configure the SDK for a workspace

> Install the Martian SDK and configure a workspace key, agent registration, and tested Git revision.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/install-and-configure/)

Python SDK · Owner/admin to create a key; scoped machine key for SDK execution

Install the Python package and create the platform connection used by Evals and red teaming. At the end, you will have a verified SDK installation, a scoped API key, and a validated tutorial configuration.

For account-free evaluation and local results, start with the [Local SDK guides](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/local-sdk.md). See [PyPI release history](https://pypi.org/project/martian-sdk/#history) for package releases.

## SDK versions and workflows

| Distribution | Version in these guides | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python package | **0.3.1** on Python 3.12 or newer | [PyPI releases](https://pypi.org/project/martian-sdk/#history) and [Local SDK setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-installation.md) |
| Local Evals UI container | **0.2.0** for Linux AMD64 | [Container registry](https://github.com/MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/pkgs/container/martian-evals) and [Docker setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#6-run-the-ui-in-a-container) |

The Python package and Docker image have separate release versions. Use the Python package for features that require SDK 0.3.1. Choose a workflow by where you want the result.

| I want to | Start here | Where the result lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run an evaluation and compare two versions without an account | [Community quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/quickstart.md) | Local result files and the packaged Evals UI |
| Check a pull request with a deterministic suite | [Run local Evals on pull requests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ci.md) | Actions job summary and selected artifacts |
| Move a local Evals store to another machine | [Export and restore Evals records](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#export-and-restore-evals-records) | A directory of JSONL files and a manifest, with known transport credentials removed |
| Save a gate against an agent and a tested revision | [Persisted CI session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/ci.md) | An enabled Martian workspace, using a scoped key |

The 0.3.1 Evals Action reports in the job summary, and each invocation evaluates the suite afresh. Portable Evals exports and pushes remove private connection settings and mask known credential values. Review the files and destination access before sharing them.

## Before you start

For an account-free Python test, follow [Run Python Evals with pytest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-pytest.md).

-   Use **Python 3.12 or newer** and Bash or Zsh on macOS, Linux, or WSL.
-   Install Git. The tutorial creates a local Git repository so a persisted CI result can name the exact committed code revision.
-   An **owner or admin** creates API keys. Running the SDK uses that key’s permissions and restrictions; the key does not grant console administration.
-   Your organization must have the compatible Backend services enabled. Hosted red teaming also needs enabled organization entitlement and configured generation/judging. Installing the package does not activate those services.
-   Obtain your organization’s approved **Backend origin**. It may differ from the browser console address. Use the origin without `/v1`, a query, or another path.

## 1\. Download the runnable tutorial and install the release

[Download the complete tutorial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/sdk/martian-sdk-tutorial.zip). Start in the directory containing that download. The following commands extract a new folder, make that folder an isolated Git repository, commit the tutorial source, and install the SDK there:

```sh
unzip martian-sdk-tutorial.zip -d martian-sdk-tutorial
cd martian-sdk-tutorial
git init -b main
git add -- .gitignore README.md demo_agent.py pytest.ini \
  support-regressions.jsonl redteam.yaml redteam.py combined_ci.py \
  key_agent_id.py github-actions.yml tests/evals
git commit -m 'Add Martian SDK tutorial'
python3 --version
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade 'martian-sdk[evals]'
martian --version
```

If Git asks for your identity, set `git config user.name 'Your Name'` and `git config user.email 'your-email@example.com'` **inside this tutorial repository**, using your own details, then repeat the commit. The extracted ZIP itself has no Git history; the commit above is what makes the later revision command meaningful.

Run the remaining local commands from this repository’s root with `.venv` active. Its relevant layout is:

```text
martian-sdk-tutorial/
  .gitignore
  demo_agent.py
  pytest.ini
  support-regressions.jsonl
  redteam.yaml
  redteam.py
  combined_ci.py
  key_agent_id.py
  github-actions.yml
  tests/evals/test_quality.py
  tests/evals/test_dataset.py
  .venv/                         # local; ignored by Git
```

`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` should identify this folder. The callback, test imports, YAML-relative callback path and CI commands all use this layout. To use an existing customer repository instead, follow the [complete copy and adaptation checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/ci.md#use-an-existing-customer-repository); copying the workflow alone is insufficient.

The final command prints your installed SDK version. The `evals` extra adds the pytest/MLflow dependencies needed for evaluations and persisted CI; base redteam support is part of the distribution. The optional `mcp` extra is for customer-side MCP integration, not a requirement for this tutorial.

Use a fresh environment when migrating from old code-bearing `martian-redteam` or `martian-evals-kit` installations. The modern package retains compatibility imports, but the examples here use `martian.evals` and `martian.redteam`.

### Use the environment in a new terminal

From your tutorial folder, activate the environment again.

```sh
source .venv/bin/activate
martian --version
```

Activation adds `.venv/bin` to the front of this shell’s `PATH`. Commands such as `python -m pip` and `martian ui` then use that environment. [Python virtual environments](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/venv.html#how-venvs-work)

## 2\. Open API-key management

1.  Sign in to the intended organization as an **owner or admin**.
2.  Select **Evals**, then **Runs**.
3.  Find the **API keys** section and select **Create key**.

![Actual SDK key metadata with four Evals and CI permissions and an agent restriction.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-api-keys.png)

The owner can manage SDK keys on Evals → Runs. This list shows permissions, restriction, expiry and a prefix; the once-shown credential was closed and is absent from the image.

API keys are managed on the Evals Runs page. If the section is absent, check the selected organization and your role before looking for another settings page.

## 3\. Choose the smallest useful permissions

In **Create API key**, enter **Key name**, set **Expires in days**, then select the required **Permissions**.

| UI permission | Capability | Needed for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read evaluation datasets and results | `evals:read` | Pulling datasets and reading evaluation results |
| Upload evaluation results | `evals:write` | Uploading locally executed dataset outputs |
| Read CI sessions | `ci:read` | Reading saved sessions and export status |
| Upload CI sessions | `ci:write` | Persisting checks and CI sessions |
| Run hosted redteam generation and judging | `redteam:run` | Hosted attack generation and judging |

![Create API key form with four Evals and CI permissions, a one-day expiry and the teaching agent restriction.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-key-form.png)

Choose the permissions and registration before creating the key.

For the complete Evals/CI tutorial, keep the four evaluation/CI permissions. Add **Run hosted redteam generation and judging** for redteam or combined runs. If that option is disabled, the dialog explains that hosted redteam is not enabled and configured; request access from your workspace administrator instead of changing credentials or retrying execution.

For the persisted CI tutorial, select the intended existing registration **by name** under **Agent restriction**. If no registration exists, complete [agent connection onboarding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md) first or have your workspace owner identify the existing demo registration to use. Running a local Python callback does not create a registration.

**All agents / standalone use** is available for an unrestricted key, but it does not identify one agent UUID for the lookup below. **Dataset restrictions** accepts one dataset name per line; an empty list permits datasets otherwise available to the key. Restrictions and permissions cannot be edited after creation.

Select **Create API key**. In **Save your API key**, save the once-shown value in your secret manager, then select **Done**. The ordinary key list contains safe metadata and a prefix, not the secret. Keep this disclosure out of screenshots, recordings, logs, and Git.

## 4\. Configure your local process

Set the approved origin. For a local tutorial, this masked prompt reads the key without putting its value in shell history:

```sh
export MARTIAN_API_URL='https://YOUR-APPROVED-BACKEND-ORIGIN'
export MARTIAN_API_TOKEN="$(python -c 'import getpass; print(getpass.getpass("Martian API key: "))')"
```

Replace the example origin with the value supplied for your workspace. HTTPS is required except loopback development. The SDK does not load `.env` automatically and does not use YAML to select a different platform origin.

The equivalent explicit Python connection is:

```python
import os
from martian import MartianConfig

config = MartianConfig(
    api_url=os.environ["MARTIAN_API_URL"],
    token=os.environ["MARTIAN_API_TOKEN"],
)
```

Supply one `MartianConfig` or the complete URL/token pair. The default request timeout is 120 seconds, within a supported 1–240-second range. Redirects and environment proxies are disabled by default. Your callback’s model/provider credentials are separate from this platform key.

## 5\. Resolve the exact CI agent UUID

With the agent-bound key loaded, run the included [key\_agent\_id.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/sdk/key_agent_id.py) helper:

```sh
MARTIAN_AGENT_ID="$(python key_agent_id.py)" && export MARTIAN_AGENT_ID
```

The helper performs the supported, read-only **`GET /v1/sdk/capabilities`** operation using your platform key and reads its `agent_id` field. Backend validates organization ownership when an agent-bound key is issued. The helper prints only that exact UUID on success; it never prints the key and never executes a target or model.

If it reports that the key is not agent-bound, create a replacement key with the intended **Agent restriction**, load the new token, and repeat. Do not invent a UUID or use a UUID from another organization.

The registration provides a label and access binding for saved CI records. The SDK still invokes `demo_agent.answer` from the committed local checkout; it does not call the registration’s remote connection. Selecting a registration does not attest that the local callback is the same binary as a deployed agent. Choose the registration deliberately with the workspace owner and describe a tutorial run as a tutorial.

Standalone dataset reads and standalone redteam need no CI agent UUID or Git revision. If you are only using those interfaces, you can omit this step.

## 6\. Validate and pin the tested revision

```sh
martian redteam validate redteam.yaml
```

Exit `0` means the YAML, catalog choices and callback reference are valid. Validation does not call a model or invoke the target callback. It does not prove platform authentication or hosted readiness.

From the same tutorial Git repository, set the tested revision and private local store for persisted CI:

```sh
git status --short
export MARTIAN_EVALS_GIT_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
export MARTIAN_EVALS_STORE_DIR="$PWD/.martian-local-mlflow"
```

Review `git status --short`: commit any intended callback, test or configuration edits before setting the revision and running the gate. Generated environments, stores and result files are ignored by the tutorial’s `.gitignore`. An agent-bound key must match the exact `MARTIAN_AGENT_ID` obtained above. When moving to your customer repository, commit the actual target code and tests there and take that repository’s revision instead.

## Verify success and handle failures

-   **Installed:** `martian --version` reports an installed release.
-   **Configured:** the origin is correct and the key is available only to the intended process or trusted CI job.
-   **Validated:** the tutorial YAML exits `0`. A later authenticated command is still required to establish service access.
-   **Permission denied:** check capabilities, agent/dataset restrictions, organization, expiration and revocation. Do not switch to an operator credential.
-   **Key lost or restrictions changed:** create a replacement, update consumers, and select **Revoke** on the old key. Revocation blocks later requests; already admitted work may finish. Issuer removal or disablement also revokes issuer keys.
-   **Network or setup failure:** preserve the safe error code/operation ID and follow [troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/troubleshooting.md). An uncertain execution is not a reason to submit the same work again.

Continue with [SDK evaluations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/evaluations.md), [one redteam probe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam.md), or [combined CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/ci.md). See [permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md) for role and capability boundaries.

---

# Run local Evals on pull requests

> Run a deterministic eval suite in GitHub Actions without a Martian account and read the result in the job summary.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/local-ci/)

Python SDK · Developer who can add a GitHub Actions workflow; no Martian account is needed

Check each pull request against a suite file and read the verdict in the GitHub Actions job summary. The example uses GitHub Actions and the [two-case support suite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#2-write-the-suite-file). Its target and checks run without a Martian account, target credentials, or a model key.

## 1\. Add your suite to the repository

Keep `evals.yaml`, `cases.jsonl`, and `agent.py` together. Run the suite with [the Local SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#3-run-the-suite) first. Keep the data synthetic when the workflow or its artifacts are public.

## 2\. Run the suite on pull requests

Save the workflow below as `.github/workflows/evals.yml`. It uses the SDK 0.3.1 Evals Action, which evaluates fresh results on each run. The job runs code from the pull request, so use the `pull_request` event with read-only permissions and no secrets.

```yaml
name: Evals
on: pull_request

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  evals:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Run the Evals suite
        id: evals
        uses: MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/.github/actions/evals@2459bee92fbcd01f9192eee60f1bdf38adac3c18 # v0.3.1
        with:
          suite: evals.yaml
          output: eval-results
      - name: Retain the summary and test report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.evals.outputs.results-written == 'true' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: eval-results
          path: |
            eval-results/summary.json
            eval-results/junit.xml
```

## 3\. Read the check and its reports

In the pull request’s **Checks** tab, open **Evals** and select the workflow run’s **Summary**. The support suite reports **2 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors**. Change `suite` to the relative path of your own suite when you are ready.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Every case passed |
| `1` | At least one case failed a check |
| `2` | A case had no verdict or the configuration was invalid |

The artifact step retains `summary.json` and `junit.xml` when the invocation writes results, even on a failed gate. Review case IDs and failure reasons before sharing the reports. Raw replies and inputs can appear in `results.jsonl` and `mlflow.db`.

## Troubleshooting

-   If only a job summary appears, check its error message. A configuration error can occur before the action writes any results.
-   If you are upgrading from the action that posted pull-request comments, remove the `github-token` and `comment-author` inputs. The report now appears in the job summary.
-   Run tests that need a target or judge credential in a separate trusted workflow. To compare a pull request to the default branch, see [baseline setup for the Evals Action](https://github.com/MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/blob/v0.3.1/docs/gate-and-ci.md#compared-with-the-last-result-of-main).

For an evaluation record tied to an agent and Git revision in your Martian workspace, follow the [workspace CI guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/ci.md).

---

# CLI command reference

> Look up Martian commands for local Evals, starting the UI, importing results, and reviewing saved reports.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/local-cli/)

Run these commands from the terminal where you [installed the SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-installation.md). In a uv project, you can prefix a command with `uv run`. For example, use `uv run martian --version`.

## Check the version and options

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Print the SDK version | `martian --version` |
| List command groups | `martian --help` |
| List evaluation commands | `martian evals --help` |
| Show options for a subcommand | `martian evals export --help` |

Use the help for your installed release when a flag differs from a guide. Replace capitalized placeholders like `FILE` or `DIR` with your paths and quote paths that contain spaces.

## Run evaluations and open the UI

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Run a [YAML suite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals-yaml.md) | `martian evals run evals.yaml` |
| Grade every case again and save a separate result | `martian evals run evals.yaml --fresh --output results-candidate` |
| Try a small set before running the whole suite | `martian evals run evals.yaml --limit 2` |
| Choose how many cases run at once | `martian evals run evals.yaml --concurrency 2` |
| Run the [local pytest example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-pytest.md) | `MARTIAN_EVALS_OFFLINE=1 martian evals run test_support.py -q` |
| Start the [local UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md) | `martian ui` |
| Open a specific data folder and port | `martian ui --data-dir ./evals-data --port 7601` |
| Start the UI without opening a browser | `martian ui --no-open` |

`martian evals run evals.yaml --data-dir ./evals-data` puts the saved run in the folder opened by `martian ui --data-dir ./evals-data`. Without an override, both use `MARTIAN_EVALS_HOME`, or `~/.martian/evals` if it is unset. The suite’s result files and the UI data folder serve different purposes.

For a YAML suite, exit code `0` means all selected cases passed. Code `1` means a check failed. Code `2` means a configuration error or a missing verdict. Use the [suite guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#4-read-the-results) to inspect the results.

## Import, export, and move results

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| List supported import formats | `martian evals import --help` |
| Export from the [local UI store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#export-and-restore-evals-records) | `martian evals export ./evals-export --data-dir ./evals-data` |
| Restore an export to an empty data folder | `martian evals import martian ./evals-export --data-dir ./restored-evals` |
| Copy an [MLflow store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/mlflow.md) | `martian evals import mlflow SOURCE` |
| Import [promptfoo results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/promptfoo.md) | `martian evals import promptfoo FILE` |
| Import [Inspect AI logs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/inspect.md) | `martian evals import inspect LOG` |
| Convert a promptfoo evaluation config to suite files | `martian evals convert promptfoo CONFIG` |

Use [Create and import Evals datasets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-datasets.md) for test cases such as JSON Lines or CSV. The commands above move recorded runs, stores, or tool-specific configurations.

## Look up advanced Evals commands

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Find options for saving matrix prompt versions | `martian evals prompts push --help` |
| Check how a suite grades canned replies | `martian evals audit --help` |
| Inspect a completed run for signs of grader gaming | `martian evals inspect-cheating --help` |
| Find options for constructing conversation cases | `martian evals personas --help` |
| Find options for comparing simulated and recorded conversations | `martian evals fidelity --help` |

## Read saved Red Team evidence

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Re-export an existing local run’s report | `martian redteam report RUN` |
| Compare stored baseline and candidate results | `martian redteam compare BASELINE CANDIDATE` |
| See which output formats are available | `martian redteam report --help` |

See [Read a saved report in the UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam-local.md#5-read-the-report-in-the-ui) or [Review Red Team YAML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-redteam-yaml.md).

### Findings and remediation commands

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Find open confirmed findings | `martian redteam findings list --status open --evidence confirmed` |
| Look up an inventory finding and its review history | `martian redteam findings show FINDING_ID` |
| Save a review decision | `martian redteam findings triage FINDING_ID --status accepted --comment "Reviewed with the owner"` |
| Export the scan’s PDF | `martian redteam report RUN --pdf -o review` |
| Draft a revised system prompt from a report | `martian redteam harden-prompt RUN system-prompt.txt -o candidate-prompt.txt` |
| Gate on any remediation regression | `martian redteam verify-remediation BASELINE FOLLOW_UP --fail-on-regression -o verification` |
| Start a read-only MCP connection to one project | `martian mcp --data-dir ./evals-data --project-id default` |
| Start MCP with just suite validation and deterministic checks | `martian mcp --preview-only` |

See the [Findings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-findings.md), [Remediation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-remediation.md) and [MCP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-mcp.md) guides for required builds, outputs and limits.

## Commands that use a workspace

Use `martian evals push --help` to see options for [sending finished runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#7-send-runs-to-a-martian-server). For `martian ci` and SDK credentials, see [Workspace SDK and CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md).
