# Create and import Evals datasets

> Write JSON Lines or CSV cases for a local suite, import records in the local UI, or bring in recorded runs from another tool.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/local-datasets/)

Python SDK · Local user

Use a case file for `martian evals run` or a published dataset for runs you start in the local UI. Both work on your machine with the [Local SDK installed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-installation.md).

| Goal | Format or action |
| --- | --- |
| Run a YAML suite | Point `data` at a JSON Lines or CSV case file |
| Run from the local UI | Create a draft, add or import records, then publish a dataset version |
| View results from another tool | [Import existing runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-datasets.md#3-import-existing-runs) |

## 1\. Write case files for a YAML suite

Each case needs an input and can include expectations used by the suite’s checks. Give cases stable, unique IDs so Compare can pair the same cases across runs.

Save this as `cases.jsonl`. Write one JSON object per line.

```json
{"id":"weekday-hours","input":"When does weekday support open?","expectations":{"opening":"9 a.m."}}
{"id":"saturday-hours","input":"When does Saturday support open?","expectations":{"opening":"10 a.m."}}
```

For a Python function with several arguments, use `inputs` as an object whose keys are argument names. A plain `input` becomes the `message` argument by default.

For CSV, use a header row. The runner treats columns other than `id`, `input`, and `output` as named expectations. Here the `opening` column supplies the same expectation as the JSON Lines example.

```csv
id,input,opening
weekday-hours,When does weekday support open?,9 a.m.
saturday-hours,When does Saturday support open?,10 a.m.
```

Set `data: cases.jsonl` or `data: cases.csv` in your suite. Use `expectation: opening` in a compatible check, such as `contains`. The [YAML reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals-yaml.md) shows how the suite connects them.

To grade replies you already have, include `output` for each case. The [saved-reply example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals-yaml.md#grade-saved-replies) reads those replies from disk.

## 2\. Create a dataset in the local UI

1.  Start [the local UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#1-install-and-start-the-ui), open **Datasets**, and select **New dataset**.
2.  Enter a name such as `Support hours` and select **Create draft**.
3.  Choose **Add record** to enter a case by hand. Enter **Record ID**, **Input**, and **Expected output**, then select **Add record**. To load several cases, use **Import file**.

### Import a case file

The UI imports JSON, JSON Lines, and CSV files up to 20 MiB. Use `expected_output` for the reference answer. In CSV, use the columns `id`, `input`, `expected_output`, and `status`. Imports update records with matching IDs and add the other records.

Save the following as `support-hours.jsonl`. Select **Import file**, choose the file in **Import records**, and select **Import**.

```json
{"id":"weekday-hours","input":"When does weekday support open?","expected_output":"Support opens at 9 a.m.","status":"ACTIVE"}
{"id":"saturday-hours","input":"When does Saturday support open?","expected_output":"Support opens at 10 a.m.","status":"ACTIVE"}
```

To convert the suite examples above, give each record an `expected_output` containing the full reference reply. Keep its ID and input. The UI’s exact-match check compares with that full reply. The suite’s `contains` check compares with the phrase under `expectations.opening`.

After the import finishes, confirm you have two usable records. Open a row’s **Edit** action if you need to correct an input or expected reply.

![Support hours draft with two usable cases and an import reminder.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/local-sdk-dataset-import.png)

The draft lists both imported answers and shows which cases are usable.

### Publish and select the dataset

1.  Select **Publish**, enter a rationale of at least eight characters, and confirm.
2.  In **Published datasets**, open **Support hours** and check that both records are usable.
3.  Select **Use in eval** to open the run form with this dataset. Follow [Run an eval from the local UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#4-run-an-eval-from-the-ui) to select a target and read the results.

![Published Support hours dataset with two usable records and a Use in eval button.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/local-sdk-dataset-published.png)

Open the published dataset and select Use in eval to start with these cases.

If **Publish** is disabled, check that the draft contains usable active records. For **duplicate case IDs** from the suite runner, give each case a unique ID. If a check reports a missing expectation, match the suite’s `expectation` to a key in every relevant case.

## 3\. Import existing runs

| Source | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Martian portable export | [Restore an Evals store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#export-and-restore-evals-records) |
| MLflow tracking store | [Import from MLflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/mlflow.md) |
| promptfoo result files | [Import promptfoo results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/promptfoo.md#2-import-your-results) |
| Inspect AI logs | [Import Inspect AI logs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/inspect.md) |

For a team dataset managed in the hosted console, see [Create and publish workspace datasets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md).

---

# Run evals locally with a suite file

> Run an eval suite from one YAML file on your own machine, using deterministic checks and LLM judges with your own model key.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/local-evals/)

Python SDK · Any developer; no Martian account; own model key for LLM judges

Write a suite for your own agent by combining a YAML file, test cases, and checks. The example evaluates support hours with two deterministic cases. If you have never run an eval, start with the [Community quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/quickstart.md).

## 1\. Set up your project

Open a project folder where you can save a suite and test cases together. Use Python 3.12 or newer and [install the Local SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-installation.md). Keep your virtual environment active.

The deterministic example needs no account or model key. When your target calls an external service or you [add an LLM judge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#6-add-an-llm-judge), those services receive the inputs they need.

## 2\. Write the suite file

Save `evals.yaml` in the project folder. Paths are relative to this file.

```yaml
data: cases.jsonl
target:
  file: agent.py
  function: answer
checks:
  - type: contains
    name: mentions_opening_time
    expectation: opening
output: results
```

Save two cases in `cases.jsonl`, one JSON object per line. Each case’s `expectations.opening` provides the text that must appear in its reply.

```json
{"id":"weekday-hours","input":"When does weekday support open?","expectations":{"opening":"9 a.m."}}
{"id":"saturday-hours","input":"When does Saturday support open?","expectations":{"opening":"10 a.m."}}
```

Create `agent.py` with a function that accepts the case input as `message` and returns a string.

```python
def answer(message: str) -> str:
    if "saturday" in message.casefold():
        return "Support opens at 10 a.m. on Saturdays."
    return "Support opens at 9 a.m. on weekdays."
```

Replace the function body with a call to your application when using this pattern for your own agent. If your agent already exposes an API, use an [HTTP target](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#8-test-an-agent-behind-an-http-endpoint).

## 3\. Run the suite

```sh
martian evals run evals.yaml
```

Expect **2 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors** and exit code `0`. Use the printed run code to find the result in the [local Evals UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md).

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Every case passed every check |
| `1` | At least one case failed a check |
| `2` | A case had no verdict, or the suite configuration was invalid |

## 4\. Read the results

The suite writes these files in `results`.

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `results.jsonl` | Inputs, replies, case verdicts, and the reason for each check |
| `summary.json` | Pass, fail and error counts, with pass rates and 95% intervals |
| `junit.xml` | CI report with separate failures and errors |
| `verdicts.json` | Verdicts and fingerprints for comparison, without inputs or replies |
| `mlflow.db` | Evaluation data, including traces |

```sh
python -m json.tool results/summary.json
```

Read `results.jsonl` when a case fails or has no verdict. It contains inputs and replies in clear text, like the evaluation database. Keep both private. Review failure reasons in JUnit reports before sharing them.

## 5\. Rerun a suite

A rerun can reuse saved verdicts with matching fingerprints. The fingerprint covers the case, the checks, the target, and the SDK version. Use a different output folder to compare a candidate with your original result, and use `--fresh` to evaluate every selected case.

```sh
martian evals run evals.yaml --fresh --output results-candidate
```

Open **Compare** in the [local Evals UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#compare) to pair results by case ID.

## 6\. Add an LLM judge

Use a judge when a check depends on the meaning of a reply. Copy `evals.yaml` to `evals-with-judge.yaml`. Keep `data` and `target` from the original file. Add `judge` and update `checks` and `output`.

```yaml
judge:
  model: "openai:/YOUR_JUDGE_MODEL"
  inference_params:
    temperature: 0
checks:
  - type: contains
    name: mentions_opening_time
    expectation: opening
  - type: rubric
    name: answers_the_question
    rubric: Pass when the reply clearly states when support opens on the day asked about.
output: results-judge
```

1.  Replace `YOUR_JUDGE_MODEL` with a model you have access to.
2.  Set your provider’s key in your environment. Test inputs, replies, and criteria go to this provider.

| Provider | `judge.model` | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `openai:/<model>` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI-compatible endpoint | `openai:/<model>` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_BASE` set to the endpoint’s `/v1` address |
| Amazon Bedrock OpenAI-compatible endpoint | `openai:/<Bedrock model ID>` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` set to a Bedrock API key and `OPENAI_API_BASE` set to the regional endpoint |

For example, use `https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/openai/v1` for an enabled model in that region. [Generate a short-term Bedrock key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-generate.html).

3.  Run the copy and read the judge’s reason for each case in `results-judge/results.jsonl`.

```sh
martian evals run evals-with-judge.yaml
```

The suite file supports three judge types. Use at most one of each type in a suite.

| `type` | Criteria | What the judge decides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rubric` | `rubric`: one piece of text | Pass or fail against the rubric as a whole |
| `guidelines` | `guidelines`: a list of rules | Each rule is complied with, violated or not applicable; any violation fails |
| `conditions` | `conditions`: a list of `{question, fail_when}` | The judge answers each yes/no question; you decide whether `yes` or `no` fails |

Criteria written in the suite file apply to every case. A case can carry its own instead, under the same key in its `expectations`.

For a rule-by-rule explanation, replace the rubric check with this `guidelines` check:

```yaml
  - type: guidelines
    name: answers_about_support
    guidelines:
      - "State the opening time for the day the customer asked about."
```

For an explicit yes/no question, use `conditions`. Quote `"yes"` and `"no"` so YAML reads them as strings:

```yaml
  - type: conditions
    name: mentions_an_opening_time
    conditions:
      - question: "Does the reply state a support opening time?"
        fail_when: "no"
```

These snippets replace one item under `checks`; keep the suite’s `data`, `target` and `judge` settings. Use a new output folder or `--fresh` after changing the check.

A judgment that is invalid or uncertain is reported as an **error**, never as a pass. If the provider rate-limits, the judge waits as long as the provider asks, for up to `judge.rate_limit_wait_seconds` (default 300, at most 3600), separately from the retries. Server errors and connection failures are retried up to five times by default (`judge.max_retries`). It never asks again after receiving a judgment.

## 7\. Run it in CI

Use [Run local Evals on pull requests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ci.md) for a read-only GitHub Actions workflow that uses this suite.

To keep a result tied to an agent and Git revision in a shared workspace, follow [Record CI results in a workspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/ci.md).

## 8\. Test an agent behind an HTTP endpoint

Copy the suite to `evals-http.yaml`. Keep the same cases and checks. Replace `target` with the URL, body, and response field for your endpoint. Set `output: results-http` to keep it separate from the function-based run.

```yaml
target:
  url: "http://127.0.0.1:8765/chat"
  headers:
    Authorization: "Bearer ${AGENT_API_KEY}"
  body:
    message: "{{input}}"
    session: "{{uuid}}"
  response_path: reply
```

Set `AGENT_API_KEY` in the shell that runs the suite if the endpoint needs it. For an endpoint without authentication, omit `headers`. Start your agent, then run the HTTP suite.

```sh
martian evals run evals-http.yaml
```

The SDK sends a JSON `POST` for each case. This example reads the returned text from a field such as `{"reply":"Support opens at 9 a.m. on weekdays."}`. For a chat-completions response, use `choices.0.message.content`. For a downloadable localhost agent and its dataset, see [Run an eval from the UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#4-run-an-eval-from-the-ui).

-   **Placeholders** are filled into `body` for each case. `{{input}}` is the case’s `input`. `{{inputs.NAME}}` is one value from a case’s `inputs` object. `{{uuid}}` is a new random ID, for agents that keep a conversation per session. The body must use `{{input}}` or `{{inputs.NAME}}`.
-   **Secrets stay in your environment.** `${NAME}` in `url` or in a header value is replaced from the environment when the suite loads. Only the name is in the suite file, and the value is not written to the result files. `${NAME}` is not replaced inside `body`.
-   **Case text is sent as written.** `${...}` or `{{...}}` inside a case’s input reaches your agent unchanged.
-   **One request per case.** There is no retry, redirects are not followed, and proxy settings from the environment are not used.

A URL target cannot be combined with `file` or `function`. Keep using a Python function when your agent needs another HTTP method, a body that is not JSON, several calls per case, or a secret inside the body.

The example token `demo-token` only shows how a credential is passed. Use `https` for any endpoint that is not on your own machine or network, and review a suite file from someone else before running it with your credentials loaded: the file chooses where your cases and headers are sent.

## Reference

-   [Suite YAML, HTTP targets, and checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals-yaml.md)
-   [Case file formats and local UI datasets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-datasets.md)
-   [CLI commands and run options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-cli.md)

## Failures and limits

-   **Exit code `2` before any case runs:** the suite file is invalid, a path is wrong, or the target file cannot be imported. The message names the field or file.
-   **A case with no verdict:** the target raised an error, a check could not find its expectation value, or a judge returned no usable judgment. The case is counted under **Errors**, the run exits `2`, and a rerun tries that case again.
-   **URL target, before any case runs:** a `${NAME}` variable that is not set stops the run with exit code `2` and names the setting and the variable, for example `Eval run failed: target.headers.Authorization needs the environment variable AGENT_API_KEY`. An invalid target, such as a body with no input placeholder or an unknown placeholder, is rejected the same way.
-   **URL target, during the run:** a status outside 2xx, a timeout, an address that cannot be reached, or a response with no value at `response_path` gives that case no verdict, and the run exits `2`. The case’s `error` in `results.jsonl` says why, and the command prints a count for each reason after the table. For HTTP 401, check the credentials in `target.headers`. For a connection error, confirm the service is running and check `target.url`. The reason never includes the address, a header or the response body. A Python function target reports only `the target call failed`.
-   **Judges can be wrong.** Calibrate a rubric on replies you know should pass and fail before relying on it, and prefer a deterministic check wherever the text itself decides.
-   **Judge calls cost money and leave your machine.** Each LLM check uses your provider for each case; multiple judges and transport retries add requests.
-   **Rate limits:** if errors persist after the retries, lower `--concurrency` or raise `judge.max_retries`.
-   **Not a platform record.** A local run has no Martian session, agent attribution or tested revision. It is a development and pull-request check, not a release gate recorded by Martian.
-   **Private files:** do not publish `results.jsonl` or `mlflow.db` as public artifacts.

Continue with [Python Evals with pytest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-pytest.md) for Python assertions or [local CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ci.md) to run a suite on pull requests.

---

# Evals suite YAML

> Build an evals.yaml file, look up suite fields and checks, and run it against an agent or saved replies.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/local-evals-yaml/)

An Evals suite connects a [case file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-datasets.md#1-write-case-files-for-a-yaml-suite) to a list of checks. Save it as `evals.yaml` and use the [Local SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-installation.md) to run it.

## Write a suite file

```yaml
data: cases.jsonl
target:
  file: agent.py
  function: answer
checks:
  - type: contains
    name: mentions_opening_time
    expectation: opening
output: results
```

`data` points to the cases and `target` selects the function returning replies. Each item under `checks` is a separate check. `expectation: opening` reads the `opening` value from each case. Paths are relative to the suite file. Indent nested settings with spaces and prefix list items with `-`.

The [local suite walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#2-write-the-suite-file) provides matching cases and a Python function. Run it with `martian evals run evals.yaml`.

## Suite fields

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `data` | Required path to a JSON Lines or CSV case file |
| `checks` | Required list of one or more checks with unique names |
| `case_gate` | Optional [weighted case scoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals-yaml.md#score-a-case-with-weighted-checks). Without it, all checks must pass |
| `target` | Python `file` and `function`, or an [HTTP target](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals-yaml.md#http-target). Omit it to grade saved replies |
| `judge` | Model settings for [LLM checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#6-add-an-llm-judge). Use `model` and optionally `inference_params`, `max_retries`, and `rate_limit_wait_seconds` |
| `output` | Results folder. Defaults to `results` |
| `input_key` | Argument name for a case’s plain `input`. Defaults to `message` |
| `concurrency` | Cases processed at once. Defaults to 4 |
| `repeats` | Attempts per case. Defaults to 1 |
| `combine` | How repeated results are combined. The default `all` requires all attempts to pass |

The runner rejects unknown keys. For prompt or model matrices, saved responses, and run limits, see the [SDK’s suite documentation](https://github.com/MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/blob/v0.4.0/docs/evals.md#run-a-suite-file-locally).

## HTTP target

Use these keys under `target` to send cases to your own HTTP endpoint.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | Required HTTP or HTTPS address without inline credentials |
| `body` | Required JSON body for the POST. Use `{{input}}`, `{{inputs.NAME}}`, or `{{uuid}}` in string values |
| `headers` | Optional headers |
| `response_path` | Optional dotted path to the reply. An index selects a list item, as in `choices.0.message.content`. Without a path, the SDK grades the raw response text |
| `timeout_seconds` | Per-request timeout. Defaults to 120 seconds |

A body value made entirely of a placeholder keeps the source value’s type. Use `${NAME}` in the URL or a header value to read a setting from your environment. [Configure a URL target](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-evals.md#8-test-an-agent-behind-an-http-endpoint).

## Deterministic checks

These checks evaluate replies without calling a judge.

| `type` | Settings | Passes when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains` | `values` or `expectation`. Optional `any_of` and `case_sensitive` | The reply contains the expected text |
| `not_contains` | `values` or `expectation`. Optional `case_sensitive` | The reply contains none of the given strings |
| `matches` | `pattern` | The regular expression is found in the reply |
| `not_matches` | `pattern` | The regular expression is absent from the reply |
| `is_json` | Optional `required_keys` | The reply is valid JSON and contains any required keys |
| `json_schema` | `schema` and optional `embedded: strict` | The reply matches the schema. In embedded mode, any matching object in the reply passes |
| `word_count` | `min_words`, `max_words`, or both | The reply meets the inclusive word-count bounds |
| `levenshtein` | `values` or `expectation`, with optional `max_edits` | The reply is within the edit limit of at least one reference |

Use `values` for text shared across all cases, or `expectation` to select a per-case value. For `contains`, all values must be present unless you set `any_of: true`. Text matching ignores case unless you set `case_sensitive: true`. A check name must differ from the expectation key it reads. [All deterministic checks](https://github.com/MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/blob/v0.4.0/docs/evals.md#deterministic-checks).

### Check structured replies

SDK 0.4.0 and later support `is_xml` for well-formed XML. Save the example below as `catalog-evals.yaml`.

```yaml
data: catalog-cases.jsonl
checks:
  - type: is_xml
    name: second_book_title
    required_elements: [catalog.book.1.title]
output: results-catalog
```

Save one reply in `catalog-cases.jsonl`.

```json
{"id":"catalog","input":"List two titles as XML.","output":"<catalog><book><title>First</title></book><book><title>Second</title></book></catalog>"}
```

Run `martian evals run catalog-evals.yaml` and expect one passing case. Paths start at the root. The zero-based index `1` selects the second `book` sibling. Set `fragment: true` to look for well-formed XML in surrounding prose or a code fence. Set `negate: true` to require the condition to fail.

### Score a case with weighted checks

Use SDK 0.4.0 or later. This suite requires an object with a string title inside a reply. It gives that check three times the weight of the word-count check. Each check keeps its own verdict, and the overall case passes at a weighted score of 0.75 or higher.

Save as `weighted-evals.yaml`.

```yaml
data: weighted-cases.jsonl
checks:
  - type: json_schema
    name: has_title
    embedded: strict
    schema:
      type: object
      required: [title]
      properties:
        title: {type: string}
  - type: word_count
    name: concise
    max_words: 10
case_gate:
  threshold: 0.75
  weights: {has_title: 3}
output: results-weighted
```

Save these records as `weighted-cases.jsonl`. The suite grades the saved replies without calling an agent or a model.

```json
{"id":"short","input":"Return a catalog entry.","output":"Catalog entry follows. {\"title\":\"Atlas\"}"}
{"id":"long","input":"Return a catalog entry.","output":"Here is the requested catalog entry with the title supplied for this branch: {\"title\":\"Atlas\"}"}
{"id":"wrong-type","input":"Return a catalog entry.","output":"Here is an entry: {\"title\":42}"}
```

```sh
martian evals run weighted-evals.yaml --data-dir ./evals-data
```

Expect two passing cases and one failing case, with exit code `1`. The long reply earns 0.75 because the schema check passed. The reply with the numeric title earns 0.25 because only the word-count check passed. [Weighted gates and assertion sets](https://github.com/MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/blob/v0.4.0/docs/evals.md#weighted-case-gates)

## Grade saved replies

To evaluate replies you already have, save this record as `saved-cases.jsonl`.

```json
{"id":"weekday-hours","input":"When does weekday support open?","output":"Support opens at 9 a.m.","expectations":{"opening":"9 a.m."}}
```

Save this as `saved-evals.yaml` next to it.

```yaml
data: saved-cases.jsonl
checks:
  - type: contains
    name: mentions_opening_time
    expectation: opening
output: results-saved
```

```sh
martian evals run saved-evals.yaml
```

Expect one passing case. The reply comes from `output`, and this check needs no agent or model call. Keep all recorded replies in the case file when omitting `target`.

## Fix configuration errors

-   If the YAML parser reports a line and column, check indentation, missing quotes, and the dash before each check.
-   If the runner reports an unknown field, check its spelling and nesting. For example, `expectation` belongs to a check and `expectations` belongs to a case.
-   If a check reports a missing expectation, add that key to each relevant case or use shared `values`.

See the [CLI command reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-cli.md) for run flags and result paths.

---

# Review and triage local findings

> Review findings across saved Red Team scans, save triage decisions, and export evidence for another reviewer or CI.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/local-findings/)

Python SDK · Developer or reviewer using the single-user local workbench

SDK version

The project-wide Findings view requires SDK 0.4.0 or later and its [bundled workbench](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/local-sdk.md#open-the-bundled-workbench).

Use Findings to review the security observations recorded in one local project. A developer or reviewer can use saved scans without a Martian account or model key.

## Before you start

-   Start the [bundled workbench](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/local-sdk.md#open-the-bundled-workbench) with the folder that holds your saved scans.
-   Have a finished scan in the project, such as one saved by the CLI or [imported from a Promptfoo or Marsfoo archive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/promptfoo-redteam.md#group-saved-scans-by-target).

## 1\. Find the evidence

1.  Select the local project, then open **Red Team → Findings**. Search by finding, target or method. Filter by severity, status, category, vulnerability type, evidence, target or recurrence.
2.  To start with one scan, open its run report and select **Findings of this run**. **Clear filters** keeps that scan selected. **Show all scans** restores the project-wide view. The totals above the table always describe the project.
3.  Open a finding by name. Use its observations to see when it occurred, the method and evidence level, and the saved scan or attempt. Re-judging a scan reviews its previous observations and adds no new observation to the inventory.

The inventory groups observations by recorded target identity, vulnerability, finding type and objective. Legacy network scans with no recorded route, network targets using custom headers, query parameters or inline credentials, and stdio MCP targets stay scoped to their own runs. Assign an explicit target key when grouping imports for a known target.

## 2\. Save a triage decision

1.  Choose a status such as **Open**, **Accepted**, **Fixed**, **False positive** or **Ignored**. Add a comment and, if needed, override the severity. **Restore scan severity** returns to the highest severity recorded for the finding.
2.  Select **Save triage**. The decision appears in the history and the original scan evidence, severity and results remain available. Refresh to read the saved entry.
3.  If the browser loses the response to a save, select **Retry saved triage**. It resends the same decision and reuses the original history entry if the first request saved it.

![An accepted review retained in the published SDK workbench after refreshing the finding.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/sdk-preview-finding-triage.png)

An accepted review retained in the published SDK workbench after refreshing the finding.

**Seen after fix** marks a later observation. The cutoff is the review time for a manual fix and the follow-up scan’s start time for a [verified fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-remediation.md#3-verify-a-fix-against-a-saved-follow-up). The inventory uses scan timestamps, including for scans imported after the review.

## 3\. Export the findings or move reviews

**Export CSV** and **Export SARIF** include all findings that match the current filters, across pages. Exports include finding summaries, evidence labels and guidance. Conversations and reviewer comments stay in the local store. SARIF uses stable finding fingerprints.

**Export Colang** builds a NeMo Guardrails archive for the current filters. Choose **Colang 1.0** or **Colang 2.x**. Confirmed findings with supported message policies can produce rules. The manifest also identifies findings that need confirmation or application controls and marks dismissed findings. Review the rules before integrating them into your application.

The CLI reads the same project inventory. Set `--project-id` when using a project other than `default`. List with `--format json` to get the full ID for `FINDING_ID`.

```sh
martian redteam findings list --status open --evidence confirmed --format json --data-dir ./evals-data
martian redteam findings show FINDING_ID --data-dir ./evals-data
martian redteam findings list --status open --format sarif -o findings.sarif --data-dir ./evals-data
```

To move triage history, first restore the matching scans into the same project at the destination. Use a copy of the backed-up local data folder, [push the saved native scan files](https://github.com/MartianSecurity/martian-redteam/blob/a48b354679954a4cefab076fe1ba1c6cc0bb0120/docs/redteam-api.md#pushed-runs) to the destination’s local server, or [reimport the original Promptfoo or Marsfoo archives with the same target key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/migrate/promptfoo-redteam.md#group-saved-scans-by-target). A verified fix needs both scans. Preview the import, then apply it.

```sh
martian redteam findings export-triage --data-dir ./evals-data -o reviews.json
martian redteam findings import-triage reviews.json --data-dir ./restored-evals --dry-run
martian redteam findings import-triage reviews.json --data-dir ./restored-evals
```

The import keeps review IDs, timestamps, authors and evidence references. It reuses reviews with matching IDs and content. If a review ID conflicts or required scan evidence is missing, correct the destination and rerun the dry run. Keep the archive private because it contains review comments.

Continue to [Remediation Reports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-remediation.md) or [read local findings through MCP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-mcp.md).

---

# Install the Local SDK

> Install martian-sdk with pip or uv, activate your environment, and check the Martian CLI version.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/local-installation/)

Python SDK · Any developer; no account is needed

Install `martian-sdk[evals]` to get the Martian CLI, Evals tools, and local UI. Use Python 3.12 or newer and Bash or Zsh on macOS, Linux, or WSL. You can install the package and run deterministic Evals without a Martian account.

Choose the installer you use for the project.

-   [Install with pip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-installation.md#install-with-pip) if Python is already installed and you want a virtual environment.
-   [Install with uv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-installation.md#install-with-uv) if you use uv to manage packages or Python versions.

If the project already has a compatible virtual environment, activate it and start at the install command.

## Install with pip

From your project directory, check that `python3` is Python 3.12 or newer, then create and activate a virtual environment.

```sh
python3 --version
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade 'martian-sdk[evals]'
martian --version
```

If `python3` points to an older interpreter, use `python3.12` or another installed version at least as recent to create the virtual environment.

## Install with uv

If you need uv, follow its [installation guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). From your project directory, create and activate a virtual environment, then install the SDK.

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install --upgrade 'martian-sdk[evals]'
martian --version
```

`uv venv` can fetch Python 3.12 when it is missing. For a project you already manage with uv, record the dependency in `pyproject.toml` and use `uv run` to run Martian in its environment.

```sh
uv add 'martian-sdk[evals]'
uv run martian --version
```

## Run Martian from a new terminal

From the project directory, activate the environment again. You can then run `martian` directly.

```sh
source .venv/bin/activate
martian --help
```

If the shell reports **`martian: command not found`**, activate the environment where you installed it and run `martian --version`. In a uv project, use `uv run martian --version`. [Python SDK releases](https://pypi.org/project/martian-sdk/#history).

Run the [Community quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/quickstart.md) or find a task in the [CLI command reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-cli.md). For one-user Docker setup, see [Run the UI in a container](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MartianSecurity/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/local-ui.md#6-run-the-ui-in-a-container).
